```{r function-format_num}
#' format numeric vectors using gtsummary style number labels safely
#'
#' @param x numeric vector to be formatted
#' @param ... optional arguments passed along to label_style_number
#'
#' @returns a character vector of formatted numbers
#' @importFrom gtsummary label_style_number
#' @export
format_num <- function(x, ...) {
  # build the formatting constructor inside an isolated execution context to bypass compiler warnings
  formatter <- gtsummary::label_style_number(...)
  
  # execute the function directly on the incoming numeric elements
  formatter(x)
}
```


```{r function-add_gt_to_word}

#' Add a gtsummary objet to word doc
#'
#' @param doc word doc created as `officer::read_docx()`
#' @param gt_obj gtsummary object
#' @param title character header
#' @param landscape logical. page orientation
#' @importFrom flextable  body_add_flextable
#' @importFrom officer body_add_par body_add_break body_end_section_landscape
#'
#' @returns a word doc
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' add_gt_to_word(doc, gt_obj, title, landscape = FALSE)
#' }
add_gt_to_word <- function(doc, gt_obj, title, landscape = FALSE) {
  # Convert gtsummary to flextable
  ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(gt_obj) %>%
    flextable::autofit()
  
  # Add title and table
  doc <- doc %>%
    body_add_par(title, style = "heading 2") %>%
    body_add_flextable(ft) %>%
    body_add_par("") # spacing
  
  # Handle Orientation and Page Breaks
  if (landscape) {
    # Close the current landscape section
    doc <- doc %>% body_end_section_landscape() 
  } else {
    # If not landscape, just add a standard page break
    doc <- doc %>% body_add_break()
  }
  
  return(doc)
}

```

```{r tests-add_gt_to_word}
library(testthat)
library(officer)
library(gtsummary)
library(dplyr)
test_that("add_gt_to_word works correctly under different conditions", {
  
  # setup: create dummy data and a basic gtsummary object
  mock_df <- data.frame(
    status = c("active", "inactive", "active"),
    age = c(25, 34, 45)
  )
  mock_gt <- gtsummary::tbl_summary(mock_df, by = status)
  
  # test 1: verification of the standard portrait flow
  doc_portrait <- officer::read_docx()
  res_portrait <- add_gt_to_word(
    doc = doc_portrait, 
    gt_obj = mock_gt, 
    title = "Test Portrait Title", 
    landscape = FALSE
  )
  
  # check that an officer document object is returned
  expect_s3_class(res_portrait, "rdocx")
  
  # convert doc to content dataframe to check text insertion
  content_p <- officer::docx_summary(res_portrait)
  expect_true(any(content_p$text == "Test Portrait Title"))
  
  # test 2: verification of the landscape flow
  doc_landscape <- read_docx()
  res_landscape <- add_gt_to_word(
    doc = doc_landscape, 
    gt_obj = mock_gt, 
    title = "Test Landscape Title", 
    landscape = TRUE
  )
  
  expect_s3_class(res_landscape, "rdocx")
  
  content_l <- docx_summary(res_landscape)
  expect_true(any(content_l$text == "Test Landscape Title"))
  
  # test 3: safe verification of landscape structural layout differences
  # landscape structural blocks alter row structures or total summary elements
  expect_false(identical(nrow(content_p), nrow(content_l)))
})
```

## clean names

```{r function-clean_username}
#' clean names by removing special characters, deleting extra spaces, and converting to title case
#'
#' @param x character vector of names to clean
#'
#' @returns a vector
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{clean_username()}
clean_username <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    # remove all special characters like brackets, braces, and punctuation
    stringr::str_remove_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]]") %>%
    # collapse duplicate whitespace down to single spaces
    stringr::str_squish() %>%
    # convert the cleaned text string to title case format
    stringr::str_to_title()
}
```



## export list of gt objects/dataframes to word

```{r  function-export_list_to_word}
#' Export a list of dataframes to word
#'
#' @param table_list list of dataframes
#' @param doc_path character vector of output directory
#' @importFrom flextable  body_add_flextable
#' @importFrom officer body_add_par body_add_break 
#'
#' @returns NULL
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{export_list_to_word()}
export_list_to_word <- function(table_list, doc_path) {
  
  # initialize a new word document
  doc <- officer::read_docx()
  
  # iterate through the named list
  # .x is the table/df, .y is the name of the list element
  purrr::iwalk(table_list, function(.x, .y) {
    
    # logic to handle different table types
    if (inherits(.x, "gtsummary")) {
      # convert gtsummary to flextable
      ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(.x)
    } else {
      # treat as standard dataframe and format
      ft <- flextable::flextable(.x) %>%
        flextable::theme_booktabs() %>%
        flextable::autofit() %>%
        flextable::bold(part = "header")
    }
    
    # add the header and the table to the document
    doc <<- doc %>%
      # use the list name as a header 2
      body_add_par(.y, style = "heading 2") %>%
      body_add_flextable(ft) %>%
      # add a small spacer after each table
      body_add_par("") 
  })
  
  # save the completed document
  print(doc, target = doc_path)
}
```


## Create gtsummary table

```{r function-create_summary_table}
#' create a `gtsummary` table
#'
#' @param data dataframe
#' @param cols columns to include
#' @param labels character. labels
#' @param group_by character. grouping variable
#' @param strata character. stratifying variable
#' @param percent_type character. percents by row or column
#' @param dichotomous_as_continuous logical. treat binary 0/1  and likert scale columns as continuous
#' @param report_median logical. whether to include the median alongside the mean for continuous variables (ignored if numeric_summary_type is "sum")
#' @param label_characteristic character. custom header text for the characteristic column
#' @param round_continuous logical. whether to round continuous summaries to whole numbers instead of decimals
#' @param numeric_summary_type character. summary format for numeric columns, either "mean" or "sum"
#'
#' @returns a gtsummary object that renders across all formats natively
#' @export
create_summary_table <- function(data, 
                                 cols = dplyr::everything(), 
                                 labels = list(), 
                                 group_by = NULL,
                                 strata = NULL,
                                 percent_type = "column",
                                 dichotomous_as_continuous = FALSE,
                                 report_median = FALSE,
                                 label_characteristic = "Characteristic",
                                 round_continuous = FALSE,
                                 numeric_summary_type = c("mean", "sum")) {
  
  # validate the requested numeric summary type layout choice
  numeric_summary_type <- match.arg(numeric_summary_type)
  
  # internal helper to build the base table structure
  build_summary <- function(df) {
    
    # establish structural types for the columns
    summary_types <- list(gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "categorical")
    
    if (dichotomous_as_continuous) {
      # find columns selected by the user that are numeric but classified as categorical or dichotomous
      selected_df <- df %>% dplyr::select({{cols}})
      numeric_likert_cols <- names(selected_df)[sapply(selected_df, is.numeric)]
      
      if (length(numeric_likert_cols) > 0) {
        # explicitly convert these names into a formula assigning them to continuous format
        likert_type_list <- stats::setNames(rep(list("continuous"), length(numeric_likert_cols)), numeric_likert_cols)
        summary_types <- c(summary_types, likert_type_list)
      }
      
      # add standard dichotomous continuous conversion selector rule
      summary_types <- c(summary_types, list(gtsummary::all_dichotomous() ~ "continuous"))
    }
    
    # assign the aggregate display token macro string based on chosen structural type
    continuous_stat <- if (numeric_summary_type == "sum") {
      "{sum}"
    } else if (report_median) {
      "{mean} ({median})"
    } else {
      "{mean}"
    }
    
    # set continuous digit precision based on rounding argument choice
    continuous_digits <- if (round_continuous || numeric_summary_type == "sum") 0 else 1
    
    # build out the core table skeleton structures
    base_summary <- df %>%
      dplyr::select({{cols}}, dplyr::any_of(group_by)) %>%
      gtsummary::tbl_summary(
        by = dplyr::any_of(group_by),
        label = labels,
        percent = percent_type,
        type = summary_types,
        statistic = list(
          gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ continuous_stat,
          gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
        ),
        digits = list(
          # lower case comments without dots or dashes
          # dynamically switch style format if handling raw numbers vs percentage indexes
          gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ function(x) {
            val <- na.omit(x)
            # bypass index scaling logic entirely if calculating aggregate total sums
            if (numeric_summary_type == "sum") {
              return(gtsummary::style_number(x, digits = continuous_digits))
            }
            if (length(val) > 0 && max(val) > 1) {
              return(gtsummary::style_number(x, digits = continuous_digits))
            } else {
              return(paste0(gtsummary::style_number(x * 100, digits = continuous_digits), "%"))
            }
          },
          gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
        ),
        missing = "no"
      )
    
    # append an overall summary tracking column explicitly if group_by is actively passed
    # modify label to read total instead of overall when running a sum aggregation table
    if (!is.null(group_by)) {
      overall_label <- if (numeric_summary_type == "sum") "**Total**" else "**Overall**"
      base_summary <- base_summary %>%
        gtsummary::add_overall(last = FALSE, col_label = overall_label)
    }
    
    # append global metadata and formatting styles down the remaining pipeline
    # omit adding the sample size n column if calculating running metric sums
    if (numeric_summary_type != "sum") {
      base_summary <- base_summary %>% gtsummary::add_n()
    }
    
    base_summary %>%
      gtsummary::bold_labels() %>%
      # selectively target non overall group headers using all_stat_cols helper wrapper
      # lower case comments without dots
      gtsummary::modify_header(
        label ~ paste0("**", label_characteristic, "**"),
        gtsummary::all_stat_cols(stat_0 = FALSE) ~ "**{level}**"
      ) %>%
      gtsummary::modify_footnote(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ NA) %>%
      gtsummary::modify_table_body(function(x) {
        attr(x, "table_styling")$columns_width <- NULL
        return(x)
      })
  }
  
  # logic to handle stratification cleanly
  raw_gtsummary <- if (!is.null(strata)) {
    data %>%
      gtsummary::tbl_strata(
        strata = dplyr::all_of(strata),
        .tbl_fun = ~ build_summary(.x)
      )
  } else {
    build_summary(data)
  }
  
  return(raw_gtsummary)
}
```

```{r function-create_survey_summary_table}
#' create a `gtsummary` table from a survey design object
#'
#' @param data a survey design object created via the survey package
#' @param cols columns to include
#' @param labels character. labels
#' @param group_by character. grouping variable
#' @param strata character. stratifying variable
#' @param percent_type character. percents by row or column
#' @param dichotomous_as_continuous logical. treat binary 0/1 and likert scale columns as continuous
#' @param report_median logical. whether to include the median alongside the mean for continuous variables (ignored if numeric_summary_type is "sum")
#' @param label_characteristic character. custom header text for the characteristic column
#' @param round_continuous logical. whether to round continuous summaries to whole numbers instead of decimals
#' @param numeric_summary_type character. summary format for numeric columns, either "mean" or "sum"
#'
#' @returns a gtsummary object that renders across all formats natively
#' @export
create_survey_summary_table <- function(data, 
                                        cols = dplyr::everything(), 
                                        labels = list(), 
                                        group_by = NULL,
                                        strata = NULL,
                                        percent_type = "column",
                                        dichotomous_as_continuous = FALSE,
                                        report_median = FALSE,
                                        label_characteristic = "Characteristic",
                                        round_continuous = FALSE,
                                        numeric_summary_type = c("mean", "sum")) {
  
  # validate the requested numeric summary type layout choice
  numeric_summary_type <- match.arg(numeric_summary_type)
  
  # internal helper to build the base survey table structure
  build_survey_summary <- function(srv_obj) {
    
    # establish structural types for the columns
    summary_types <- list(gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "categorical")
    
    if (dichotomous_as_continuous) {
      # extract the raw dataframe variables from inside the survey design object matrix boundary
      extracted_df <- srv_obj$variables %>% dplyr::select({{cols}})
      numeric_likert_cols <- names(extracted_df)[sapply(extracted_df, is.numeric)]
      
      if (length(numeric_likert_cols) > 0) {
        # explicitly convert these names into a formula assigning them to continuous format
        likert_type_list <- stats::setNames(rep(list("continuous"), length(numeric_likert_cols)), numeric_likert_cols)
        summary_types <- c(summary_types, likert_type_list)
      }
      
      # add standard dichotomous continuous conversion selector rule
      summary_types <- c(summary_types, list(gtsummary::all_dichotomous() ~ "continuous"))
    }
    
    # assign the aggregate display token macro string based on chosen structural type
    continuous_stat <- if (numeric_summary_type == "sum") {
      "{sum}"
    } else if (report_median) {
      "{mean} ({median})"
    } else {
      "{mean}"
    }
    
    # set continuous digit precision based on rounding argument choice
    continuous_digits <- if (round_continuous || numeric_summary_type == "sum") 0 else 1
    
    # build out the core survey table skeleton structures using tbl_svysummary
    base_summary <- srv_obj %>%
      gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
        by = dplyr::any_of(group_by),
        include = c({{cols}}, dplyr::any_of(group_by)),
        label = labels,
        percent = percent_type,
        type = summary_types,
        statistic = list(
          gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ continuous_stat,
          gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n_unweighted} ({p}%)"
        ),
        digits = list(
          # lower case comments without dots
          # dynamically switch style format if handling raw numbers vs percentage indexes
          gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ function(x) {
            val <- na.omit(x)
            # bypass index scaling logic entirely if calculating aggregate total sums
            if (numeric_summary_type == "sum") {
              return(gtsummary::style_number(x, digits = continuous_digits))
            }
            if (length(val) > 0 && max(val) > 1) {
              return(gtsummary::style_number(x, digits = continuous_digits))
            } else {
              return(paste0(gtsummary::style_number(x * 100, digits = continuous_digits), "%"))
            }
          },
          gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
        ),
        missing = "no"
      )
    
    # append an overall summary tracking column explicitly if group_by is actively passed
    if (!is.null(group_by)) {
      base_summary <- base_summary %>%
        gtsummary::add_overall(last = FALSE, col_label = "**Overall**")
    }
    
    # append global metadata and formatting styles down the remaining pipeline
    base_summary %>%
      gtsummary::bold_labels() %>%
      # selectively target non overall group headers using all_stat_cols helper wrapper
      gtsummary::modify_header(
        label ~ paste0("**", label_characteristic, "**"),
        gtsummary::all_stat_cols(stat_0 = FALSE) ~ "**{level}**"
      ) %>%
      gtsummary::modify_footnote(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ NA) %>%
      gtsummary::modify_table_body(function(x) {
        attr(x, "table_styling")$columns_width <- NULL
        return(x)
      })
  }
  
  # logic to handle stratification cleanly across survey configurations
  raw_gtsummary <- if (!is.null(strata)) {
    data %>%
      gtsummary::tbl_strata(
        strata = dplyr::all_of(strata),
        .tbl_fun = ~ build_survey_summary(.x)
      )
  } else {
    build_survey_summary(data)
  }
  
  return(raw_gtsummary)
}
```


## create a listing table using `gtreg{}`

```{r function-create_listing_table}

#' create `gtreg` table listing of data
#'
#' @param data dataframe
#' @param cols columns to include
#' @param labels character. labels
#' @param group_by character. grouping variable 
#'
#' @returns a list
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#'\dontrun{create_listing_table()}
create_listing_table <- function(data,
                                 cols = dplyr::everything(),
                                 labels = list(),
                                 group_by = NULL) {
  data %>%
    {
      if (!is.null(group_by))
        dplyr::arrange(., .data[[group_by]])
      else
        .
    } %>%
    dplyr::select({{ cols }}, dplyr::any_of(group_by)) %>%
    gtreg::tbl_listing() %>%
    gtsummary::bold_labels()
}

```

## clean a vector of strings

```{r function-clean_string}
# clean string

#' clean string of spaces and non alphanumeric characters and make lower case
#'
#' @param x a vector of characters
#'
#' @returns a vector
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{clean_String('Nachola124')}


clean_string <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    as.character() %>%
    stringr::str_to_lower() %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]", "") %>%
    stringr::str_trim()
}
```

## clean phone number

```{r function-clean_phone_number}
#' clean phone number by adding 254 prexif
#'
#' @param x dataframe
#' @param col character vector of phone number columns
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
clean_phone_number <- function(x, col = c("reg_num", "telephone_number", "proxy_num")) {
  x %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(col),
        ~ {
          # convert elements to character format to guarantee stable evaluation
          char_vec <- base::as.character(.x)
          
          dplyr::case_when(
            # match format missing a leading country code or standard zero index
            base::nchar(char_vec) == 9  ~ base::paste0("254", char_vec),
            # match format structured with a leading single local digit zero index
            base::nchar(char_vec) == 10 ~ base::gsub("^0", "254", char_vec),
            # fall back and preserve raw entries unchanged if lengths do not match
            TRUE ~ char_vec
          )
        }
      )
    )
}
```

## process payroll

```{r function-process_payroll}
#' clean payroll data
#'
#' @param x dataframe
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
process_payroll <- function(x) {
  # find columns matching pattern to pass safely to standard selectors
  drop_cols <- base::grep("^x", base::names(x), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  
  # target accounting columns requiring explicit type casting
  numeric_targets <- c(
    "cash_transfer_kes", 
    "mpesa_sending_charges", 
    "mpesa_withdrawal_charges", 
    "total_amount_kes"
  )
  
  x %>%
    # drops matching columns safely if they exist, ignores if empty
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(drop_cols)) %>%
    
    # defensive filter check: if "no" exists, filters out NAs; if missing, lets all rows pass
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any(dplyr::any_of("no"), ~ !base::is.na(.x)) | !("no" %in% base::names(.))) %>%
    
    # defensive mutate check: targets telephone_number safely using any_of
    dplyr::mutate(
      # dplyr::across(
      #   dplyr::any_of("telephone_number"),
      #   ~ base::gsub("^254", "0", base::as.character(.x))
      # ),
      # defensive numeric conversion check: loops through specified financial column keys if present
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(numeric_targets),
        ~ base::as.numeric(.x)
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        any_of(c("name_of_beneficiary", "name_of_proxy", "telephone_number", "id_number")),
        clean_username
      )
    ) %>% clean_phone_number()
}
```



## recode beneficiary camps to known refugee camps

```{r function-clean_camp}
#' clean recode beneficiary camp 
#'
#' @param x dataframe
#' @param col_name character column with camp names, defaults to 'ben_camp'
#' @param partner_col character column with partner organization names, defaults to 'reforgp'
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @importFrom dplyr case_when all_of across
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{clean_camp(x, col_name = "ben_camp", partner_col = "reforgp")}
clean_camp <- function(x, col_name = "ben_camp", partner_col = "reforgp") {
  x %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(col_name), ~ dplyr::case_when(
        # use the .data pronoun to dynamically evaluate the partner column name input
        grepl("\\bna\\b|N/A|kawangware|kayole|kasarani|kangemi|kikuyu|home", .x, ignore.case = TRUE) & grepl("HIAS", .data[[partner_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Nairobi",
        grepl("^k|^rece", .x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kakuma",
        grepl("^nai|east|urban|umoja|rongai|settl", .x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Nairobi",
        grepl("^daga|ley$|^ifo|f0|fo|^haga|^v|dad|daad", .x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Daadab",
        is.na(.x) ~ "Nairobi",
        TRUE ~ .x
      ))
    )
}
```


## get group columns

```{r function-get_group_cols}
#' Extract column names from a data dictionary based on structural boundaries
#'
#' @param dict dataframe representing the data dictionary
#' @param name_col string. The column containing the variable names to extract
#' @param vulnerability_df a dataframe with vulnerability categories
#' @param vulnerability_class character vector of vulnerability class
#'
#' @returns a character vector of column names
#' @export
get_group_cols <- function(dict, vulnerability_df, vulnerability_class = "physio", name_col = "name") {
  
  df <- vulnerability_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      grepl(vulnerability_class, label, ignore.case = TRUE)
    )
  dict %>%
    dplyr::filter(n >= df$n & n < df$n_end) %>%
    # remove true NAs and any literal "NA" character strings
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!rlang::sym(name_col)) & !!rlang::sym(name_col) != "NA") %>%
    dplyr::pull(!!rlang::sym(name_col))
}
```

```{r function-check_esr_registrations}
# registrations appearing in ESR
#' Title
#'
#' @param data1 dataframe. registration data
#' @param data2 dataframe. ESR data
#'
#' @returns a dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{check_esr_registrations(data1 = df_clean, data2 = df_esr)}
check_esr_registrations <- function(data1 = df_clean, data2 = df_esr) {

  
  # 1. prepare lookup keys from data2
  # combine names and clean id and phone for matching
  data2_prepared <- data2 %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      full_name_clean = clean_string(paste(first_name, middle_name, last_name)),
      first_surname = clean_string(paste(first_name, last_name)),
      first_secname = clean_string(paste(first_name, middle_name)),
      id_clean        = clean_string(id_number1),
      phone_clean     = clean_string(phone_number)
    )
  
  lookup_ids    <- unique(data2_prepared$id_clean)
  lookup_names  <- unique(data2_prepared$full_name_clean)
  lookup_names1  <- unique(data2_prepared$first_surname)
  lookup_names2  <- unique(data2_prepared$first_secname)
  lookup_phones <- unique(data2_prepared$phone_clean)
  
  # 2. apply matching logic to data1
  data1 %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_in_second_dataset = case_when(
        # check by id number
        clean_string(ben_id_number) %in% lookup_ids ~ "yes",
        
        # check by phone number using reg_num_phone
        clean_string(reg_num_phone) %in% lookup_phones ~ "yes",
        
        # check by combined name
        clean_string(ben_name) %in% lookup_names ~ "yes",
        clean_string(ben_first_surname) %in% lookup_names1 ~ "yes",
        clean_string(ben_first_secname) %in% lookup_names2 ~ "yes",
        
        # default to no if no matches are found
        TRUE ~ "no"
      )
    )
}
```

## get standard villages

```{r function-get_standard_villages}
#' separate villages collapsed by forward slash ("|")
#'
#' @param data1 dataframe. ESR/partner data
#' @param data2 dataframe. registration data
#'
#' @returns a dataframe
#' @importFrom stringr str_extract str_replace_all
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{get_standard_villages(data1 = df_partner, data2 = df_clean)}
get_standard_villages <- function(data1 = df_partner, data2 = df_clean) {
  
  # get unique reference villages and sort by length descending
  # this ensures long names are matched before substrings
  villages <- unique(data2$village2)
  villages_sorted <- villages[order(nchar(villages), decreasing = TRUE)]
  
  # escape special characters and collapse for regex
  village_pattern <- paste(stringr::str_escape(villages_sorted), collapse = "|")
  
  data1 %>%
    # separate rows based on the forward slash
    # this turns "village1/village2" into two distinct rows
    tidyr::separate_rows(village, sep = "/") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # extract the standard name using the pattern
      village2 = str_extract(village, regex(village_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)),
      # capitalize first letters of village names as per your requirement
      # this handles slashes if they appear in the result
      village2 = str_replace_all(village2, "(^|/)([a-z])", function(m) toupper(m))
    )
}
```

## find extra agency records

```{r function-find_extra_agency_records}
#' find unique extra records in a matched dataset missing from the reference payroll
#'
#' @param matched_df dataframe containing the processed matched records (e.g., df_matched)
#' @param payroll_df dataframe containing the raw reference payroll records (e.g., d_pay_out)
#' @param target_agency character string identifying the specific agency group to audit
#' @param matched_agency_col character name of the agency column in matched_df
#' @param payroll_agency_col character name of the agency column in payroll_df
#'
#' @returns a filtered dataframe containing the rogue records present only in matched_df
#' @export
find_extra_agency_records <- function(matched_df = df_matched, 
                                      payroll_df = d_pay_out, 
                                      target_agency = "ALDEF", 
                                      matched_agency_col = "enum_egency", 
                                      payroll_agency_col = "partner") {
  
  # slice down both data matrices to focus exclusively on the target agency group
  subset_matched <- matched_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[matched_agency_col]] == target_agency)
  
  subset_payroll <- payroll_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[payroll_agency_col]] == target_agency)
  
  # capture tracking records that exist in the match pool but have no match on payroll
  extra_records <- subset_matched %>%
    dplyr::anti_join(
      subset_payroll,
      by = c(
        "id_number" = "id_number",
        "telephone_number" = "telephone_number"
      )
    )
  
  return(extra_records)
}
```


## find column names in a list

```{r function-grep_columns_in_list}
#' grep column names matching a pattern across a list of dataframes
#'
#' @param df_list named list of dataframes to scan
#' @param pattern character string or regex pattern to search for
#' @param ignore_case logical. whether the search should be case-insensitive
#'
#' @returns a named list showing only the matched column names for each dataframe
#' @export
grep_columns_in_list <- function(df_list, pattern, ignore_case = TRUE) {
  
  # verify the incoming object is structurally a list format
  if (!base::is.list(df_list)) {
    base::stop("the input df_list must be a valid list object")
  }
  
  # ensure all list elements have tracking names assigned
  if (base::is.null(base::names(df_list))) {
    base::names(df_list) <- base::paste0("df_", base::seq_along(df_list))
  }
  
  # map across the list to extract matching column labels
  matched_results <- purrr::map(df_list, function(df) {
    
    # pull all column elements present in the data frame boundary matrix
    all_cols <- base::names(df)
    
    # run regular expression filter against the column metadata layer
    matching_cols <- stringr::str_subset(
      all_cols, 
      pattern = stringr::regex(pattern, ignore_case = ignore_case)
    )
    
    # return the matches if found, otherwise return null
    if (base::length(matching_cols) > 0) {
      return(matching_cols)
    } else {
      return(NULL)
    }
  })
  
  # compact down the list results to drop elements with zero matches
  purrr::compact(matched_results)
}
```

```{r function-pull_kobo_data_mpca}
#' pull data from any kobo API project and align structures dynamically
#'
#' @param url character. Kobotoolbox url
#' @param project_id character. project id
#' @param token character. project token
#'
#' @returns a clean dataframe matching manual excel column conventions universally
#' @export
pull_kobo_data_mpca <- function(
      url = Sys.getenv("kobo_url2"),
  project_id = Sys.getenv("mpca_id"),
  token = Sys.getenv("kobo_token")
){
  
  robotoolbox::kobo_setup(url = url, token = token)
  
  # pull all data rows and historical columns
  df <- robotoolbox::kobo_data(project_id, all_versions = TRUE)
  
  # force convert metadata levels into plain text strings safely
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), function(col) {
      lbls <- attr(col, "labels")
      if (!is.null(lbls)) {
        lookup <- names(lbls)
        names(lookup) <- as.character(lbls)
        col_str <- as.character(col)
        
        return(dplyr::if_else(col_str %in% names(lookup), lookup[col_str], col_str))
      }
      return(col)
    }))
  
  # 1. drop the plain 'uuid' column first to prevent naming collisions
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("uuid"))
  
  # 2. rename standard system fields to match manual clean excel structures
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      id = dplyr::any_of("_id"),
      uuid = dplyr::any_of("_uuid"),
      status = dplyr::any_of("_status"),
      submission_time = dplyr::any_of("_submission_time"),
      validation_status = dplyr::any_of("_validation_status"),
      submitted_by = dplyr::any_of("_submitted_by"),
      version = dplyr::any_of("__version__"),
      meta_root_uuid = dplyr::any_of("rootUuid")
    ) %>%
    # project agnostic: converts ALL group delimiter dots to underscores
    # handles patterns like 'a.sec_cluster' -> 'a_sec_cluster' or 'b.age' -> 'b_age'
    dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace_all(.x, "\\.", "_"))
  
  # 3. drop general platform-specific headers not in standard clean excel exports
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "_attachments",
        "_xform_id_string",
        "instanceID",
        "instanceName",
        "cordinates_latitude",
        "cordinates_longitude",
        "cordinates_altitude",
        "cordinates_precision",
        "index",
        "tags",
        "notes"
      ))
    )
  
  return(df)
}
```

## clean manual kobo excel data

```{r function-clean_kobo_excel}
#' clean manual kobo excel data to align with api structure
#'
#' @param data data.frame. the raw excel data frame (ddd)
#'
#' @returns a cleaned data frame matching the transformed api structure
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{clean_kobo_excel(ddd)}
clean_kobo_excel <- function(data) {
  
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("input must be a data frame")
  }
  
  # 1. remove trailing or leading white spaces from character columns
  cleaned_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.character), stringr::str_trim))
  
  # 2. handle potential duplicate columns before renaming
  # if both "middle_name" and "ben_reff" exist, drop the plain "ben_reff" to avoid a collision
  if ("middle_name" %in% names(cleaned_df) && "ben_reff" %in% names(cleaned_df)) {
    cleaned_df <- cleaned_df %>% dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("ben_reff"))
  }
  
  # 3. handle structural header renames to match code/value naming layout
  cleaned_df <- cleaned_df %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      # map core name metadata variations
      ben_first = dplyr::any_of("first_name"),
      ben_reff = dplyr::any_of("middle_name"),
      benf_last = dplyr::any_of("last_name"),
      data_entry_name = dplyr::any_of("name_of_person_collecting_information"),
      cordinates = dplyr::any_of("please_collect_the_beneficiary_gps_coordinates"),
      
      # convert exploded select_multiple text fields to match api value strings
      livelihood_source_dnk = dplyr::any_of("livelihood_source_dont_know"),
      livelihood_source_f_employment = dplyr::any_of("livelihood_source_formal_employment"),
      livelihood_source_frm_lvstk = dplyr::any_of("livelihood_source_farming_livestock"),
      livelihood_source_other_benflivelihood = dplyr::any_of("livelihood_source_other"),
      livelihood_source_ss_business = dplyr::any_of("livelihood_source_small_scale_business")
    )
  
  # 4. safely drop internal coordinate splits and extra tracker tags 
  cleaned_df <- cleaned_df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "cordinates_latitude",
        "cordinates_longitude",
        "cordinates_altitude",
        "cordinates_precision",
        "please_collect_the_beneficiary_gps_coordinates_latitude",
        "please_collect_the_beneficiary_gps_coordinates_longitude",
        "please_collect_the_beneficiary_gps_coordinates_altitude",
        "please_collect_the_beneficiary_gps_coordinates_precision",
        "index",
        "tags",
        "notes"
      ))
    )
  
  # 5. ensure placeholder columns exist if they are present in df_lab structure
  if ("ben_reff" %in% names(cleaned_df) && !("benf_sec" %in% names(cleaned_df))) {
    cleaned_df <- cleaned_df %>% dplyr::rename(benf_sec = ben_reff)
  }
  
  if (!"ref_priority" %in% names(cleaned_df)) {
    cleaned_df$ref_priority <- NA_character_
  }
  
  return(cleaned_df)
}
```


## categorize numerics

```{r function-cut_numeric}
#' categorize numeric cols
#'
#' @param x a vector of numeric column
#' @param breaks numeric vector of breaks
#' @param labels character vector of labels
#'
#' @returns vector
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' cut_numeric(c(1:10), c(-Inf,5, Inf), c("<=5", ">=6"))
cut_numeric <- function(
    x, 
    breaks = c(-Inf, 18, Inf), 
    labels = c("<18", ">=18")
){
  # find the true minimum value of the input vector
  min_val <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # if the minimum value is less than the first break point adjust the breaks and labels
  if (min_val < breaks[1]) {
    breaks <- c(min_val, breaks)
    labels <- c(paste(min_val, "-", breaks[2] - 1), labels)
  }
  
  out <- cut(
    x,
    # breaks now safely includes the true minimum value
    breaks = breaks,
    # updated labels matching the intervals
    labels = labels,
    # include the lowest value and make intervals right open
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    right = FALSE
  )
  return(out)
}
```

## export gtsummary object to excel workbook

```{r function-export_to_excel_formatted}
#' Export/write gtsummary output to excel workbook
#'
#' @param list_of_objects list of `gtsummary` object
#' @param file_name character. output filename and associated path
#'
#' @returns NULL
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{export_to_excel_formatted()} 
export_to_excel_formatted <- function(
    list_of_objects,
    file_name = paste0("UNOCHA_Summary_Report_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx")
) {
  
  # create the workbook object
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  
  # define styles
  neg_style <- createStyle(fontColour = "#FF0000", textDecoration = "bold")
  # style for bolding the row headers (the first column)
  bold_header_style <- createStyle(textDecoration = "bold")
  
  # iterate through the named list
  purrr::iwalk(list_of_objects, function(obj, sheet_name) {
    
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
    
    # conversion logic
    df_to_write <- if (inherits(obj, "gtsummary")) {
      as_tibble(obj)
    } else {
      as.data.frame(obj)
    }
    
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, df_to_write)
    
    # 1. bold the row headers (first column)
    # rows starts at 2 to skip the excel header row
    openxlsx::addStyle(
      wb, 
      sheet_name, 
      style = bold_header_style, 
      cols = 1, 
      rows = 2:(nrow(df_to_write) + 1), 
      gridExpand = TRUE
    )
    
    # 2. apply red color coding for negative values
    openxlsx::conditionalFormatting(
      wb, 
      sheet_name, 
      cols = 1:ncol(df_to_write), 
      rows = 2:(nrow(df_to_write) + 1), 
      rule = "< 0", 
      style = neg_style
    )
    
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol(df_to_write), widths = "auto")
  })
  
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, file = file.path("output", file_name), overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

## add a new sheet to existing workbook

```{r function-export_to_excel_appended}
#' Export a sheet to existing workbook
#'
#' @param list_of_objects list of `gtsummary` object
#' @param sheetname character. worksheet name
#' @param file_name character. output file name
#' @param output_dir character. output directory
#'
#' @returns NULL
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{export_to_excel_appended()}
export_to_excel_appended <- function(
    list_of_objects = df_target_p,
    sheetname = "Target and Registered ESR",
    file_name = paste0("UNOCHA_Summary_Report_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx"),
    output_dir = "output"
) {
  
  # create output dir
  if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
    dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # build full path safely
  file_path <- file.path(output_dir, basename(file_name))
  
  message("Using file path: ", normalizePath(file_path, mustWork = FALSE))
  
  # load existing workbook OR create new
  if (file.exists(file_path)) {
    
    message("Loading existing workbook...")
    
    wb <- tryCatch(
      openxlsx::loadWorkbook(file_path),
      error = function(e) {
        message("Failed to load workbook: ", e$message)
        openxlsx::createWorkbook()
      }
    )
    
  } else {
    
    message("Workbook does not exist. Creating new workbook...")
    wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
    
  }
  
  # excel sheet name limit
  sheetname <- substr(sheetname, 1, 31)
  
  # remove existing sheet if present
  if (sheetname %in% names(wb)) {
    openxlsx::removeWorksheet(wb, sheetname)
  }
  
  addWorksheet(wb, sheetname)
  
  # styles
  header_style <- createStyle(
    fontSize = 12,
    textDecoration = "bold",
    fontColour = "#0066A1"
  )
  
  bold_row_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold")
  
  neg_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(
    fontColour = "#FF0000",
    textDecoration = "bold"
  )
  
  current_row <- 1
  
  purrr::iwalk(list_of_objects, function(obj, list_name) {
    
    df_to_write <- if (inherits(obj, "gtsummary")) {
      as_tibble(obj)
    } else {
      as.data.frame(obj)
    }
    
    # section title
    openxlsx::writeData(
      wb,
      sheet = sheetname,
      x = list_name,
      startRow = current_row
    )
    
    openxlsx::addStyle(
      wb,
      sheet = sheetname,
      style = header_style,
      cols = 1,
      rows = current_row
    )
    
    current_row <<- current_row + 1
    
    # write table
    openxlsx::writeData(
      wb,
      sheet = sheetname,
      x = df_to_write,
      startRow = current_row,
      headerStyle = bold_row_style
    )
    
    # bold first column
    if (nrow(df_to_write) > 0) {
      
      openxlsx::addStyle(
        wb,
        sheet = sheetname,
        style = bold_row_style,
        cols = 1,
        rows = (current_row + 1):(current_row + nrow(df_to_write)),
        gridExpand = TRUE,
        stack = TRUE
      )
      
      openxlsx::conditionalFormatting(
        wb,
        sheet = sheetname,
        cols = 1:ncol(df_to_write),
        rows = (current_row + 1):(current_row + nrow(df_to_write)),
        rule = "<0",
        style = neg_style
      )
    }
    
    current_row <<- current_row + nrow(df_to_write) + 3
  })
  
  # autofit
  openxlsx::setColWidths(
    wb,
    sheet = sheetname,
    cols = 1:50,
    widths = "auto"
  )
  
  # save
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(
    wb,
    file = file_path,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
  
  message("Workbook saved successfully.")
}
```

## get duplicates

```{r function-get_duplicates}
#' get duplicate beneficiaries on select variables
#'
#' @param x dataframe
#' @param vars_to_check character vector of variables to check
#' @param phone_var character vector. phone number variable for hard check
#' @param name_var character vector. name of respondent
#' @importFrom dplyr group_by across n n_distinct filter any_of ungroup distinct
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{get_duplicates()}
get_duplicates <- function(
    x,
    vars_to_check = c("benef_name", "ben_number"),
    phone_var = "ben_number",
    name_var = "benef_name"
){
  
  # 1. find phone sharing: same phone, different names
  phone_sharing <- x %>%
    group_by(across(any_of(phone_var))) %>%
    filter(n() > 1 & n_distinct(across(any_of(name_var))) > 1)
  
  # 2. find name sharing: same name, different phones
  name_sharing <- x %>%
    group_by(across(any_of(name_var))) %>%
    filter(n() > 1 & n_distinct(across(any_of(phone_var))) > 1)
  
  # 3. find exact duplicates across the vars_to_check
  exact_dups <- x %>%
    group_by(across(any_of(vars_to_check))) %>%
    filter(n() > 1)
  
  # combine all instances and remove overlapping rows
  res <- bind_rows(phone_sharing, name_sharing, exact_dups) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # sort by the primary variables for easy review
  res %>%
    arrange(across(any_of(vars_to_check)))
}
```

## get distinct

```{r function-get_distinct}
#' get distinct beneficiaries on select variables
#'
#' @param x dataframe
#' @param vars_to_check character vector of columns to check
#' @param phone_var character vector of phone number column
#' @param name_var character vector of respondent name
#' @importFrom dplyr group_by across n n_distinct filter any_of ungroup distinct select pull row_number bind_rows slice
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{get_distinct()}
get_distinct <- function(
    x,
    vars_to_check = c("benef_name", "ben_number"),
    phone_var = "ben_number",
    name_var = "benef_name"
){
  # capture exact duplicates and instances of shared name with different phones
  anomalies <- x %>%
    mutate(temp_id = row_number()) %>%
    {
      bind_rows(
        # scenario 2 shared name different phones
        group_by(., across(any_of(name_var))) %>% 
          filter(n() > 1 & n_distinct(across(any_of(phone_var))) > 1),
        
        # scenario 3 exact duplicates
        group_by(., across(any_of(vars_to_check))) %>% 
          filter(n() > 1)
      )
    } %>%
    distinct(temp_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  # isolate clean rows that dont participate in those loops
  clean_data <- x %>%
    mutate(temp_id = row_number()) %>%
    filter(!(temp_id %in% anomalies$temp_id))
  
  # resolve the anomalies by keeping just the first instance per unique variable combo
  resolved_anomalies <- anomalies %>%
    group_by(across(any_of(vars_to_check))) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # bind clean entries and resolved entries back together
  bind_rows(clean_data, resolved_anomalies) %>%
    arrange(temp_id) %>%
    select(-temp_id)
}
```

## plot bar

```{r function-plot_bar}
#' plot bar graphs with automatic summary calculations
#'
#' @param data dataframe
#' @param x_var character vector x-axis variable
#' @param y_var character vector variable to calculate mean or proportion on
#' @param type character type of calculation: "count", "proportion", or "mean"
#' @param fill_col character vector of hex color code for fill
#' @param title character vector of title
#' @param subtitle character vector of subtitle
#' @param x_lab character vector of label for x-axis
#' @param y_lab character vector of label for y-axis
#' @importFrom rlang ensym as_label
#' @importFrom dplyr filter group_by summarize mutate ungroup
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_col geom_text labs scale_y_continuous expansion theme_minimal theme element_blank element_text
#' @importFrom scales percent comma
#'
#' @returns a ggplot object
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{plot_bar(data, x_var = "job_type", type = "count")}
plot_bar <- function(data, 
                     x_var, 
                     y_var = NULL, 
                     type = c("count", "proportion", "mean"),
                     fill_col = "#0066A1",
                     title = "variable distribution", 
                     subtitle = NULL, 
                     x_lab = NULL, 
                     y_lab = NULL) {
  
  type <- match.arg(type)
  x_sym <- rlang::ensym(x_var)
  x_char <- rlang::as_label(x_sym)
  
  # drop missing values from the grouping variable
  data <- data %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!x_sym))
  
  # standardizing labels based on the calculation metric
  if (is.null(y_lab)) {
    y_lab <- switch(type,
                    "count" = "count",
                    "proportion" = "proportion",
                    "mean" = "mean")
  }
  
  # internal data processing engine
  if (!is.null(y_var)) {
    y_sym <- rlang::ensym(y_var)
    
    if (type == "mean") {
      summary_df <- data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(!!x_sym) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(metric = round(mean(!!y_sym, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = !!x_sym, y = metric)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = scales::comma(metric, accuracy = 0.01)),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
      
    } else if (type == "proportion") {
      summary_df <- data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(!!x_sym) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(
          metric = if (is.numeric(!!y_sym) || is.logical(!!y_sym)) {
            mean(!!y_sym == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
          } else {
            mean(!is.na(!!y_sym), na.rm = TRUE)
          }, 
          .groups = "drop"
        )
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = !!x_sym, y = metric)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = scales::percent(metric, accuracy = 0.1)),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
      
    } else if (type == "count") {
      summary_df <- data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(!!x_sym) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(metric = sum(!!y_sym, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
        dplyr::mutate(pct = metric / sum(metric, na.rm = TRUE))
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = !!x_sym, y = metric)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(scales::comma(metric), " (", scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
    }
    
  } else {
    # case when no y variable is supplied (calculating straight counts/proportions of rows)
    summary_df <- data %>%
      dplyr::count(!!x_sym) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(pct = n / sum(n))
    
    if (type == "proportion") {
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = !!x_sym, y = pct)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1)),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
    } else {
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = !!x_sym, y = n)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(scales::comma(n), " (", scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
    }
  }
  
  # chart polishing and design options
  p <- p +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = if(is.null(x_lab)) x_char else x_lab,
      y = y_lab
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "#231F20"),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, color = "#58595B"),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "#231F20"),
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "#231F20"),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(color = "#231F20")
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r function-plot_bar_top_n}
#' plot bar graphs for top n frequencies
#'
#' @param data dataframe
#' @param x_var character vector x-axis variable
#' @param y_var character vector variable to calculate mean or proportion on
#' @param type character type of calculation: "count", "proportion", or "mean"
#' @param n_top integer maximum number of highest value categories to display
#' @param fill_col character vector of hex color code for fill
#' @param title character vector of title
#' @param subtitle character vector of subtitle
#' @param x_lab character vector of label for x-axis
#' @param y_lab character vector of label for y-axis
#' @importFrom rlang ensym as_label
#' @importFrom tidyr separate_rows
#' @importFrom dplyr filter group_by summarize mutate slice_max ungroup desc
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_col geom_text labs scale_y_continuous scale_x_discrete expansion theme_minimal theme element_blank element_text
#' @importFrom scales percent comma
#' @importFrom forcats fct_reorder
#'
#' @returns a ggplot object
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{plot_bar_top_n(data, x_var = "job_type", type = "count", n_top = 10)}
plot_bar_top_n <- function(data, 
                           x_var, 
                           y_var = NULL, 
                           type = c("count", "proportion", "mean"),
                           n_top = 10,
                           fill_col = "#0066A1",
                           title = "top variable distribution", 
                           subtitle = NULL, 
                           x_lab = NULL, 
                           y_lab = NULL) {
  
  type <- match.arg(type)
  x_sym <- rlang::ensym(x_var)
  x_char <- rlang::as_label(x_sym)
  
  # auto expand multiple response space separated text strings if present
  # if (is.character(data[[x_char]])) {
  #   data <- data %>% tidyr::separate_rows(!!x_sym, sep = " ")
  # }
  # 
  # drop missing values from the grouping variable
  data <- data %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!x_sym))
  
  # standardizing labels based on the calculation metric
  if (is.null(y_lab)) {
    y_lab <- switch(type,
                    "count" = "count",
                    "proportion" = "proportion",
                    "mean" = "mean")
  }
  
  # internal data processing engine
  if (!is.null(y_var)) {
    y_sym <- rlang::ensym(y_var)
    
    if (type == "mean") {
      summary_df <- data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(!!x_sym) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(metric = round(mean(!!y_sym, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
        dplyr::slice_max(order_by = metric, n = n_top, with_ties = FALSE)
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(!!x_sym, dplyr::desc(metric)), y = metric)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = scales::comma(metric, accuracy = 0.01)),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
      
    } else if (type == "proportion") {
      summary_df <- data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(!!x_sym) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(metric = mean(!!y_sym == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
        dplyr::slice_max(order_by = metric, n = n_top, with_ties = FALSE)
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(!!x_sym, dplyr::desc(metric)), y = metric)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = scales::percent(metric, accuracy = 0.1)),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
      
    } else if (type == "count") {
      summary_df <- data %>%
        dplyr::group_by(!!x_sym) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(metric = sum(!!y_sym, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
        dplyr::mutate(pct = metric / sum(metric, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        dplyr::slice_max(order_by = metric, n = n_top, with_ties = FALSE)
      
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(!!x_sym, dplyr::desc(metric)), y = metric)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(scales::comma(metric), " (", scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
    }
    
  } else {
    # case when no y variable is supplied (calculating straight counts/proportions of rows)
    summary_df <- data %>%
      dplyr::count(!!x_sym) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) %>%
      dplyr::slice_max(order_by = n, n = n_top, with_ties = FALSE)
    
    if (type == "proportion") {
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(!!x_sym, dplyr::desc(pct)), y = pct)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1)),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
    } else {
      p <- ggplot2::ggplot(summary_df, ggplot2::aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(!!x_sym, dplyr::desc(n)), y = n)) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = fill_col, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.75) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(scales::comma(n), " (", scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
          vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
        )
    }
  }
  
  # chart polishing and design options
  p <- p +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = if(is.null(x_lab)) x_char else x_lab,
      y = y_lab
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "#231F20"),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, color = "#58595B"),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "#231F20"),

      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(color = "#231F20")
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```

## patchwork grid plots

```{r function-patchwork_grid}
#' patchwork a list of plots with headers for sections arranged left to right with unified axes labels
#'
#' @param plot_list list of ggplot objects
#' @param section_headers character vector of headers to place above sections
#' @param plots_per_section integer number of plots that belong under each header
#' @param nrow integer number of rows for the internal plot grids, defaults to 1
#'
#' @returns a patchwork layout object
#' @importFrom patchwork wrap_elements wrap_plots plot_annotation
#' @importFrom ggplot2 labs theme element_text margin element_blank
#' @export
patchwork_grid <- function(plot_list, section_headers, plots_per_section = 1, nrow = 1) {
  
  # validate that we have enough headers for the plots provided
  num_sections <- ceiling(length(plot_list) / plots_per_section)
  if (length(section_headers) < num_sections) {
    stop("not enough section_headers provided for the number of plot groups")
  }
  
  # extract global axis labels from the first plot before stripping them
  global_x_lab <- plot_list[[1]]$labels$x
  global_y_lab <- plot_list[[1]]$labels$y
  
  # strip inner labels to prevent repeating clutter across the panels
  clean_plots <- lapply(plot_list, function(p) {
    p + ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
  })
  
  wrapped_sections <- list()
  
  # process plots group by group to wrap them under a styled section header
  for (i in seq_len(num_sections)) {
    
    # isolate the subset of plots for the current section
    start_idx <- ((i - 1) * plots_per_section) + 1
    end_idx <- min(i * plots_per_section, length(clean_plots))
    sub_plots <- clean_plots[start_idx:end_idx]
    
    # assemble the sub-grid for this specific section arranged by row
    section_grid <- patchwork::wrap_plots(sub_plots, nrow = nrow)
    
    # wrap the sub-grid as an element and attach a clean overarching title
    wrapped_sections[[i]] <- patchwork::wrap_elements(panel = section_grid) +
      ggplot2::labs(title = section_headers[i]) +
      ggplot2::theme(
        plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
          face = "bold", 
          size = 14, 
          color = "#231F20", 
          margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 10, t = 5)
        )
      )
  }
  
  # stitch all header-managed sections horizontally side-by-side
  final_layout <- patchwork::wrap_plots(wrapped_sections, nrow = 1) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      caption = global_x_lab, # uses caption style at bottom for clean centered x-axis label alignment
      theme = ggplot2::theme(
        plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, color = "#231F20", hjust = 0.5, margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 10))
      )
    )
  
  return(final_layout)
}
```


## add custom total

```{r function-add_custom_total}
#' calculate column-wise totals
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{add_custom_total()}
add_custom_total <- function(df) {
  # calculate totals
  totals <- df %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      Village = "Total",
      # only sum unique targeted values per village to avoid double counting
      `Targeted BNF` = base::sum(unique(`Targeted BNF`), na.rm = TRUE),
      `Registered BNF` = sum(`Registered BNF`, na.rm = TRUE),
      Variance = sum(Variance, na.rm = TRUE),
      `ESR Households` = sum(`ESR Households`, na.rm = TRUE),
      partner = NA
    )
  
  # combine with original data
  out <- bind_rows(df, totals)
  
  return(out)
}
```

## collapse villages

```{r function-collapse_villages}
#' collapse villages that share targets, separating by /
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{collapse_villages()}
collapse_villages <- function(df) {
  df_collapsed <- df %>%
    # group by the columns where you want to identify duplicates
    dplyr::group_by(`Targeted BNF`, `ESR Households`, partner) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      # collapse village names with a slash
      village = paste(unique(village), collapse = " / "),
      # sum the registered beneficiaries
      `Registered BNF` = sum(`Registered BNF`, na.rm = TRUE),
      # keep the group order clean
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    # relocate columns to match your original structure
    dplyr::select(village, `Targeted BNF`, `ESR Households`, partner, `Registered BNF`)
  
  return(df_collapsed)
}
```

## find partial matches

```{r function-get_partial_matches}
#' find partial matches between focal and beneficiary
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#' @param focal character vector of focal variable
#' @param beneficiary character vector of beneficiary variable
#'
#' @returns a dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{get_partial_matches()}
get_partial_matches <- function(df, focal = "focal_name", beneficiary = "benef_name") {
  df %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_partial = {
        f_raw <- .data[[focal]]
        b_raw <- .data[[beneficiary]]
        
        # 1 early exit check for missing values or empty strings
        if (is.na(f_raw) || is.na(b_raw) || f_raw == "" || b_raw == "" || f_raw == "NA" || b_raw == "NA") {
          FALSE
        } else {
          f_str <- as.character(f_raw)
          b_str <- as.character(b_raw)
          
          # 2 basic substring check first using base r grepl to avoid vector length bugs
          matched <- grepl(b_str, f_str, fixed = TRUE) | grepl(f_str, b_str, fixed = TRUE)
          
          # 3 if basic check fails look for out of order word inclusion
          if (isTRUE(matched)) {
            matched
          } else {
            # clean and split both strings into words
            f_words <- unlist(stringr::str_split(f_str, "\\s+"))
            b_words <- unlist(stringr::str_split(b_str, "\\s+"))
            
            # identify which name is shorter by token count
            if (length(f_words) <= length(b_words)) {
              short_words <- f_words
              long_str <- b_str
            } else {
              short_words <- b_words
              long_str <- f_str
            }
            
            # verify if every word of the shorter name exists in the longer string
            all(purrr::map_lgl(short_words, ~ grepl(.x, long_str, fixed = TRUE)))
          }
        }
      }
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup()
}
```

```{r function-get_partial_matches_extend}
#' find partial matches and map the single best-matching focal name onto dataframe 2
#'
#' @param df1 dataframe containing the focal variable (source of matched names)
#' @param df2 dataframe containing the beneficiary variable (target destination)
#' @param focal character name of the focal variable column in df1
#' @param beneficiary character name of the beneficiary variable column in df2
#' @param min_shared_words integer minimum number of unique words that must match to trigger a connection
#'
#' @returns dataframe 2 with an appended 'name_possible' column containing the highest probability match from df1
#' @export
get_partial_matches_extend <- function(df1, df2, focal = "focal_name", beneficiary = "benef_name", min_shared_words = 2) {
  
  # create unique row tracking keys to link matching vectors back safely
  df1_clean <- df1 %>% dplyr::mutate(`..row_id_df1..` = dplyr::row_number())
  df2_clean <- df2 %>% dplyr::mutate(`..row_id_df2..` = dplyr::row_number())
  
  # extract vectors directly from dataframes using base subsetting to bypass join name changes
  focal_vec <- df1_clean[[focal]]
  benef_vec <- df2_clean[[beneficiary]]
  
  # build a row-by-row logical evaluation matrix for all combinations
  match_grid <- base::expand.grid(
    row_df1 = base::seq_along(focal_vec),
    row_df2 = base::seq_along(benef_vec)
  )
  
  # map across combinations using vector indexes rather than data frame strings
  is_partial_vec <- purrr::map2_lgl(match_grid$row_df1, match_grid$row_df2, ~ {
    f_raw <- focal_vec[.x]
    b_raw <- benef_vec[.y]
    
    # early exit check for missing values or empty strings
    if (base::is.na(f_raw) || base::is.na(b_raw) || f_raw == "" || b_raw == "" || f_raw == "NA" || b_raw == "NA") {
      FALSE
    } else {
      f_str <- base::as.character(f_raw)
      b_str <- base::as.character(b_raw)
      
      # basic substring check first using base r grepl to avoid vector length bugs
      matched <- base::grepl(b_str, f_str, fixed = TRUE) || base::grepl(f_str, b_str, fixed = TRUE)
      
      if (base::isTRUE(matched)) {
        matched
      } else {
        # clean and split both strings into unique words
        f_words <- base::unique(base::unlist(stringr::str_split(f_str, "\\s+")))
        b_words <- base::unique(base::unlist(stringr::str_split(b_str, "\\s+")))
        
        # calculate intersect count of matching string tokens across both word arrays
        shared_tokens <- base::intersect(f_words, b_words)
        
        # enforce condition tracking threshold counts to capture out of order permutations
        base::length(shared_tokens) >= min_shared_words
      }
    }
  })
  
  # filter combination map down to verified indexes only
  valid_matches <- match_grid[is_partial_vec, ]
  
  # link valid matches back to strings and calculate Jaro-Winkler proximity metrics
  matches_mapped <- valid_matches %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      name_possible = focal_vec[row_df1],
      target_benef  = benef_vec[row_df2],
      # compute probability score between 0 and 1 using jaro winkler metric
      match_prob = stringdist::stringsim(name_possible, target_benef, method = "jw")
    ) %>%
    # group by the df2 row index to isolate competing candidates
    dplyr::group_by(row_df2) %>%
    # keep only the single highest ranking match, choosing the first if tied
    dplyr::slice_max(match_prob, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(row_df2, name_possible)
  
  # join matched values onto df2 and drop internal row indexing trackers
  df2_clean %>%
    dplyr::left_join(matches_mapped, by = c("..row_id_df2.." = "row_df2")) %>%
    dplyr::select(-`..row_id_df2..`)
}
```


## get personally identifying columns

```{r function-get_pii}
#' Get personally identifying columns
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#' @param vars string of identifying columns
#'
#' @returns a list of 3 dataframes: identifying, de-identified, and original df
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{get_pii()}
get_pii <- function(
    df = df_clean,
    vars = c("lat", "long", "name", "mobile", "gps", "phone", "enum_num$", "^(enum|reg|ben|proxy|sec)_.*(name|num|id)")
){
  cols <- paste(vars, collapse = "|")
  df_pii <- df %>% select(
    grep(cols, names(.))
  )
  df_depii <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      -grep(cols, names(.))
    )
  out <- list(df_pii, df_depii, df) %>%
    purrr::set_names(c("personaly-identifying", "de-identified", "original-data"))
  return(out)
}
```

## export a list to excel

```{r function-write_list_to_excel}
#' export a named list of data frames to an excel workbook
#' @param df_list a named list of data frames
#' @param file_path character string for the output path
#' @returns NULL
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{write_list_to_excel()}
write_list_to_excel <- function(df_list, file_path) {
  
  # create a new workbook object
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  
  # define a professional header style
  header_style <- createStyle(
    fgFill = "#4F81BD", 
    halign = "center", 
    textDecoration = "bold",
    fontColour = "white",
    border = "bottom"
  )
  
  # iterate through the named list
  # .x is the dataframe, .y is the name of the list element
  purrr::iwalk(df_list, function(.x, .y) {
    
    # add a new worksheet with the name of the list element
    # excel sheet names are limited to 31 characters
    sheet_name <- substr(.y, 1, 31)
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
    
    # write the data to the sheet
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, .x, headerStyle = header_style)
    
    # adjust column widths to fit content automatically
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol(.x), widths = "auto")
    
    # freeze the top row for easier navigation
    openxlsx::freezePane(wb, sheet_name, firstRow = TRUE)
  })
  
  # save the workbook to the specified path
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

## flatten dm object

```{r function-flatten_dm_by_names}
#' flatten all tables within a dm object into a list of data frames
#'
#' @param dm_obj a dm data model object
#'
#' @returns a named list of flattened data frames
#' @export
flatten_dm_by_names <- function(dm_obj) {
  # extract the structural table names directly from the dm object
  tbl_names <- base::names(dm_obj)
  
  # loop through the valid names to flatten each table
  df_list <- base::lapply(tbl_names, function(name) {
    dm::dm_flatten_to_tbl(dm_obj, !!name)
  })
  
  # reapply the names to the output list
  names(df_list) <- tbl_names
  
  return(df_list)
}
```

```{r function-preprocess_reg}
#' preprocess unocha registrations
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#' @importFrom dm dm_flatten_to_tbl
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate group_by case_when if_else filter bind_rows distinct
#'
#' @returns a dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{preprocess_reg()}
#' 

preprocess_reg <- function(df){
  df_out <- df %>% 
  dm_flatten_to_tbl(main)

df_out <- df_out %>%
  mutate(across(where(labelled::is.labelled), as.character))
df_out <- df_out %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    village = case_when(
      grepl("chini", village, ignore.case = T) & grepl(
        "kalakacha", sublocation, ignore.case = T
      ) ~ "Kalakacha Chini",
      TRUE ~ village
    )
  )
df_out <- df_out %>%
  mutate(
    village = case_when(
      grepl("Emmaus|Kirengender", village, ignore.case = T) ~ "Kirengender",
      grepl("salama|Kajificheni", village, ignore.case = T) ~ "Salama",
      grepl("kalkacha_juu", village, ignore.case = T) ~ "Kalakacha Juu",
      TRUE ~ village
    )
#     troublesome
    ,
    enum_egency = case_when(
      grepl("mitobini", village, ignore.case = T) &
      grepl("pgi", enum_egency, ignore.case = T) ~ "ALDEF",
      # grepl("Milimani", village, ignore.case = T) & 
      #   date(start) >= date("2026-05-13") ~ "ALDEF",
      # grepl("kurole", village, ignore.case = T) ~ "ALDEF",
      grepl("elwachu", village, ignore.case = T) ~ "ALDEF",
      TRUE ~ enum_egency
    )
  )

df_out <- df_out %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    ben_first_surname = paste(first_name, third_name),
    ben_first_secname = paste(first_name, second_name)
  )

df_out <- df_out %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    HHH_age_calc = if_else(
      !is.na(resp_age), resp_age, HHH_age
    )
  )

df_out <- df_out %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(
    c("county", "subcounty", "ward", "sublocation", "village")
  ), ~ gsub("_", " ", .x)))

df_out <- df_out %>%
  mutate(
    proxy_name = stringr::str_squish(
      paste(
        dplyr::coalesce(name_proxy_first, ""),
        dplyr::coalesce(name_proxy_second, ""),
        dplyr::coalesce(name_proxy_third, "")
      )
    ) 
  )


df_out <- df_out %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
    dplyr::any_of(
      c(
        "county",
        "subcounty",
        "ward",
        "sublocation",
        "village",
        "ben_name",
        "proxy_name"
      )
    ),
    ~ stringr::str_to_title(stringr::str_squish(.x))
  ))

df_out <- df_out %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_category = cut_numeric(HHH_age_calc),
    hh_size_category = cut_numeric(
      hh_size,
      breaks = c(1, 3, 6, 10, Inf),
      labels = c("1 - 2", "3 - 5", "6 - 9", ">= 10")
    ),
    hh_disabl_category = cut_numeric(
      hh_disability_count,
      breaks = c(0,1, 3, 5, Inf),
      labels = c("0", "1 - 2", "3 - 4", ">= 5")
    )
  )

  
df_out <- df_out %>%
  labelled::set_variable_labels(
    age_category = "Household\n Head Age",
    HHH_chronic = "HH Head\n Chronic illness",
    HHM_chronic = "HH Member\n Chronic illness",
    average_income = "Monthly Income",
    hh_size = "Household Size",
    hh_size_category = "Household Size",
    FCSGName = "Food Consumption\n Score",
    eligibility = "Eligibility",
    enum_egency = "Agency",
    enum_name = "Enumerator\n first name",
    first_name = "respondent\n first name",
    reg_num = "Respondent Phone",
    trust_proxy = "Trust proxy",
    enum_egency = "Partner",
    proxy_num_consent = "proxy consent",
    name_proxy_first = "proxy\n first name",
    proxy_num = "proxy mobile",
    proxy_relation = "proxy relation",
    HHM_disability = "Household\n disability",
    HHH_chronic = "Household\nchronic illness"
  )

# registration started May 3 ----------------------------------------------

 
  
  # distinct(
  #   ben_name, reg_num, ben_id_number, .keep_all = T
  # ) %>%
  # distinct(
  #   reg_num, ben_id_number, .keep_all = T
  # ) %>% 
  
# reg_num can be NA but distinct() would only pick one row


}
```

```{r function-preprocess}
#' preprocess unocha registrations
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#' @importFrom dm dm_flatten_to_tbl
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate group_by case_when if_else filter bind_rows distinct
#'
#' @returns a dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{preprocess()}
#

preprocess <- function(df){
  df_out <- df %>% mutate(across(where(labelled::is.labelled), as.character))

  df_out <- df_out %>% dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(
    c("county", "subcounty", "ward", "sublocation", "village")
  ), ~ gsub("_", " ", .x)))
  df_out <- df_out %>% mutate(proxy_name = clean_username(
    paste(
      dplyr::coalesce(name_proxy_first, ""),
      dplyr::coalesce(name_proxy_second, ""),
      dplyr::coalesce(name_proxy_third, "")
    )
  ))
  df_out <- df_out %>% dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
    dplyr::any_of(
      c(
        "county",
        "subcounty",
        "ward",
        "sublocation",
        "village",
        "ben_name",
        "proxy_name"
      )
    ), clean_username
  ))
  df_out <- df_out %>% dplyr::mutate(
    age_category = cut_numeric(HHH_age_final),
    hh_size_category = cut_numeric(
      hh_size,
      breaks = c(1, 3, 6, 10, Inf),
      labels = c("1 - 2", "3 - 5", "6 - 9", ">= 10")
    ),
    hh_disabl_category = cut_numeric(
      hh_disability_count,
      breaks = c(0, 1, 3, 5, Inf),
      labels = c("0", "1 - 2", "3 - 4", ">= 5")
    )
  )
  df_out <- df_out %>% labelled::set_variable_labels(
    age_category = "Household\n Head Age",
    HHH_chronic = "HH Head\n Chronic illness",
    HHM_chronic = "HH Member\n Chronic illness",
    average_income = "Monthly Income",
    hh_size = "Household Size",
    hh_size_category = "Household Size",
    FCSGName = "Food Consumption\n Score",
    eligibility = "Eligibility",
    enum_egency = "Agency",
    enum_name = "Enumerator\n first name",
    first_name = "respondent\n first name",
    reg_num = "Respondent Phone",
    trust_proxy = "Trust proxy",
    enum_egency = "Partner",
    proxy_num_consent = "proxy consent",
    name_proxy_first = "proxy\n first name",
    proxy_num = "proxy mobile",
    proxy_relation = "proxy relation",
    HHM_disability = "Household\n disability",
    HHH_chronic = "Household\nchronic illness"
  )
  df_out
}
```

## slice reg data

```{r function-slice_reg}
#' slice registration to match starting dates
#'
#' @param df dataframe
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{slice_reg()}
slice_reg <- function(df){
  df_out <- df %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
#     start of reg
    start >= lubridate::date("2026-05-03")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !(
    lubridate::as_date(start) <= lubridate::date("2026-05-06") & 
    grepl("SND", enum_egency, ignore.case = TRUE)
  )
  )
  df_out
}
```

```{r function-get_edit_data}
#' Read partner registration edit files
#'
#' @param partner character string of partners e.g., "PGI" 
#' @param cols_exclude character vector of columns to exclude from edits
#' @param sheet_name character vector of workbook sheet name
#'
#' @returns dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{get_edit_data()}
get_edit_data <- function(
    partner = "PGI",
    cols_exclude = c("village", "ben_name"),
    sheet_name = NULL
){
  p_file <- list.files(
    file.path(here::here(),"edits"), pattern = partner, full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  if(!is.null(sheet_name)){
    sheet_f <- sheet_name
  }else{
    sheet_f <- readxl::excel_sheets(p_file)
  }
  
  df <- readxl::read_excel(p_file, sheet = sheet_f) %>%
    clean_names()   %>% mutate(
      ben_name = stringr::str_squish(ben_name) %>% stringr::str_to_title()
    ) 
  df_1 <- df %>%
    
    # left_join(
    #   df_out %>% 
    #   #   filter(
    #   #   grepl("Tana", county, ignore.case = T)
    #   # ) %>%
    #     select(
    #     ben_name, ben_id_number
    #   )
    # ) %>% 
    filter(
      !grepl(paste(cols_exclude, collapse = "|"), var_to_change)
    )
  return(df_1)
}
```
