## Proportional to size random sample

```{r function-draw_pps_sample}
#' Draw PPS Household Sample
#'
#' @param data Household-level data frame.
#' @param county_var County variable name.
#' @param village_id_var Village identifier variable name.
#' @param allocation_df County allocation table.
#' @param alloc_size_var County sample size variable.
#' @param seed Random seed.
#'
#' @return Sampled household data frame.
#' @export
draw_pps_sample <- function(
    data,
    county_var = "county",
    village_id_var = "village",
    allocation_df,
    alloc_size_var = "sample",
    seed = as.numeric(Sys.Date())
){
  
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # ----------------------------
  # STEP 1: PPS village allocation
  # ----------------------------
  
  village_alloc <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(
          c(county_var, village_id_var)
        )
      ),
      name = "village_size"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      allocation_df,
      by = county_var
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(county_var)
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      
      county_total = sum(village_size),
      
      raw_alloc =
        (.data[[alloc_size_var]] *
           village_size) /
        county_total,
      
      base_alloc = floor(raw_alloc),
      
      frac = raw_alloc - base_alloc,
      
      remaining =
        first(.data[[alloc_size_var]]) -
        sum(base_alloc),
      
      sample_alloc =
        base_alloc +
        as.integer(
          dplyr::row_number(
            dplyr::desc(frac)
          ) <= remaining
        )
      
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  
  # ----------------------------
  # STEP 2: Sample village-by-village
  # ----------------------------
  
  sampled <- village_alloc %>%
    
    dplyr::group_split(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(
          c(county_var, village_id_var)
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    
    purrr::map_dfr(function(v){
      
      n_take <- v$sample_alloc[[1]]
      
      hh <- data %>%
        dplyr::semi_join(
          v,
          by = c(
            county_var,
            village_id_var
          )
        )
      
      dplyr::slice_sample(
        hh,
        n = min(
          n_take,
          nrow(hh)
        )
      )
      
    })
  
  sampled
}

```

## proportional to size sample Hamilton redistribution

```{r function-draw_pps_hamilton}
#' Draw a Sample of Households Proportional to Village Size
#'
#' This function selects a stratified random sample of individual household rows
#' from within counties. The probability of a household being selected is
#' proportional to the total size (household count) of the village it belongs to,
#' using the Hamilton (largest remainder) method for allocation. After initial
#' allocation, any village falling below \code{min_village_sample} has its
#' allocation lifted to the minimum by borrowing units from the most oversampled
#' donor villages within the same county.
#'
#' @param data A data frame containing raw household-level records.
#' @param county_var A bare or quoted column name identifying the county stratum.
#' @param village_id_var A bare or quoted column name identifying the unique village.
#' @param allocation_df A data frame containing two columns: the county identifier
#'   and the allocated household sample size for that county.
#' @param alloc_size_var A bare or quoted column name in \code{allocation_df}
#'   indicating the target sample size for each county.
#' @param seed An integer used to initialise the pseudo-random number generator
#'   for reproducible sampling. Defaults to the numeric representation of the
#'   current system date.
#' @param min_village_sample A single integer specifying the minimum number of
#'   households that must be sampled from any village. Villages initially allocated
#'   fewer than this value borrow units from the most oversampled villages in the
#'   same county. The effective minimum is capped at the village's actual household
#'   count, so small villages are never over-sampled. Defaults to \code{8L}.
#'
#' @return A data frame with the same columns as \code{data}, containing only the
#'   selected household rows. Villages with a final allocation of zero are excluded
#'   from the output entirely.
#'
#' @details
#' \strong{Allocation (step 1 — Hamilton / largest remainder):}
#' For each county, each village receives a proportional raw allocation
#' \eqn{n_v = N_{county} \times (s_v / S_{county})}, where \eqn{s_v} is the
#' village household count and \eqn{S_{county}} is the county total. Allocations
#' are floored and fractional remainders are distributed one unit at a time to the
#' villages with the largest fractional parts until the county target is met.
#'
#' \strong{Redistribution (step 2 — minimum floor):}
#' Redistribution is performed independently within each county. Donor villages —
#' those whose allocation exceeds their own effective minimum — are sorted in
#' descending order of surplus and drained greedily until the total deficit of
#' sub-minimum villages is recovered or the donor pool is exhausted. A
#' \code{\link[base]{warning}} is issued when a county cannot fully satisfy the
#' minimum for all its villages.
#'
#' \strong{Sampling (step 3):}
#' Within each village, households are drawn via simple random sampling without
#' replacement using random uniform ordering. Villages with a final
#' allocation of zero are silently dropped.
#'
#' @seealso \code{\link[dplyr]{slice_sample}}, \code{\link[dplyr]{group_modify}}
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr count across any_of left_join group_by mutate ungroup group_modify filter arrange row_number select
#' @importFrom rlang .data sym !!
#' @importFrom stats runif
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # dummy raw household data
#' raw_households <- data.frame(
#'   county_id  = rep(c("County_A", "County_B"), each = 10),
#'   village_id = c(rep("V1", 3), rep("V2", 7), rep("V3", 4), rep("V4", 6)),
#'   household_id = paste0("HH_", 1:20)
#' )
#'
#' # household sample size targets per county
#' target_allocations <- data.frame(
#'   county_id   = c("County_A", "County_B"),
#'   sample_size = c(20, 25)
#' )
#'
#' # run reproducible PPS household sampling with an 8-household village minimum
#' pps_household_sample <- draw_pps_sample(
#'   data               = raw_households,
#'   county_var         = "county_id",
#'   village_id_var     = "village_id",
#'   allocation_df      = target_allocations,
#'   alloc_size_var     = "sample_size",
#'   seed               = 123,
#'   min_village_sample = 8L
#' )
#' }
draw_pps_hamilton <- function(
    data,
    county_var         = "county",
    village_id_var     = "village",
    allocation_df,
    alloc_size_var     = "sample",
    seed               = as.numeric(Sys.Date()),
    min_village_sample = 8L
) {
  
  # preserve random seed state if it exists to maintain reproducibility safely
  if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) {
    old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)
    on.exit(assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = .GlobalEnv))
  }
  
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # convert input column names safely to standard strings
  county_str <- as.character(substitute(county_var))
  if (!county_str %in% names(data)) county_str <- county_var
  
  village_str <- as.character(substitute(village_id_var))
  if (!village_str %in% names(data)) village_str <- village_id_var
  
  # hamilton pps allocation
  village_alloc <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(c(county_str, village_str))),
      name = "village_size"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(allocation_df, by = county_str) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(county_str))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      county_total = sum(.data$village_size),
      raw_alloc    = .data[[alloc_size_var]] * .data$village_size / .data$county_total,
      sample_alloc = floor(.data$raw_alloc),
      remainder    = .data[[alloc_size_var]][1] - sum(floor(.data$raw_alloc)),
      frac         = .data$raw_alloc - floor(.data$raw_alloc),
      sample_alloc = .data$sample_alloc +
        ifelse(rank(-.data$frac, ties.method = "first") <= .data$remainder, 1L, 0L)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  
  # minimum size redistribution
  village_alloc <- village_alloc %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(county_str))) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(function(county_df, key) {
      
      alloc   <- county_df$sample_alloc
      
      # enforce the floor to be exactly min_village_sample capped at available population
      eff_min <- pmin(min_village_sample, county_df$village_size)
      
      deficit_idx <- which(alloc < eff_min)
      if (length(deficit_idx) == 0L) return(county_df)
      
      deficit        <- eff_min[deficit_idx] - alloc[deficit_idx]
      total_deficit  <- sum(deficit)
      surplus        <- pmax(alloc - eff_min, 0L)
      total_surplus  <- sum(surplus)
      
      if (total_surplus == 0L) {
        warning(
          "County '", key[[1]], "': not enough surplus to satisfy minimum of ",
          min_village_sample, " for all villages. Lifting as much as possible."
        )
      }
      
      donor_order <- order(-surplus)
      remaining   <- min(total_deficit, total_surplus)
      
      for (i in donor_order) {
        if (remaining <= 0L) break
        give      <- min(surplus[i], remaining)
        alloc[i]  <- alloc[i] - give
        remaining <- remaining - give
      }
      
      recovered <- min(total_deficit, total_surplus)
      for (j in seq_along(deficit_idx)) {
        if (recovered <= 0L) break
        give                  <- min(deficit[j], recovered)
        alloc[deficit_idx[j]] <- alloc[deficit_idx[j]] + give
        recovered             <- recovered - give
      }
      
      county_df$sample_alloc <- alloc
      county_df
    }) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  
  # sample households within each village
  # join final target allocation boundaries back to full population dataset rows
  joined_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      dplyr::select(village_alloc, dplyr::any_of(c(county_str, village_str, "sample_alloc"))),
      by = c(county_str, village_str)
    )
  
  # shuffle and slice rows matching exact targets without using group modify
  sampled <- joined_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$sample_alloc) & .data$sample_alloc > 0L) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(c(county_str, village_str)))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(rand_draw_order = stats::runif(dplyr::n())) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.data$rand_draw_order, .by_groups = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number() <= .data$sample_alloc) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("sample_alloc", "rand_draw_order")))
  
  return(sampled)
}

```


## Stratified sampling

```{r function-draw_strs_sample}
#' Draw a Stratified Simple Random Sample of Households
#'
#' This function selects a stratified simple random sample of individual household 
#' rows from within counties. Every household within a given county has an equal 
#' probability of selection, independent of village size.
#'
#' @param data A data frame containing raw household-level records.
#' @param county_var The bare or quoted column name identifying the county stratum.
#' @param allocation_df A data frame containing two columns: the county identifier 
#'   and the allocated household sample size for that county.
#' @param alloc_size_var The bare or quoted column name in `allocation_df` 
#'   indicating the target sample size.
#' @param seed An integer value used to initialize the pseudo-random number generator 
#'   for reproducible sampling. Defaults to `42`.
#'
#' @return A data frame containing the individually selected household rows.
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr group_by mutate ungroup inner_join arrange row_number filter across any_of desc n
#' @importFrom rlang sym
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # dummy raw household data
#' raw_households <- data.frame(
#'   county_id = rep(c("County_A", "County_B"), each = 10),
#'   village_id = c(rep("V1", 3), rep("V2", 7), rep("V3", 4), rep("V4", 6)),
#'   household_id = paste0("HH_", 1:20)
#' )
#'
#' # household sample size targets per county
#' target_allocations <- data.frame(
#'   county_id = c("County_A", "County_B"),
#'   sample_size = c(2, 3)
#' )
#'
#' # run reproducible stratified simple random sampling
#' strs_sample <- draw_strs_sample(
#'   data = raw_households,
#'   county_var = "county_id",
#'   allocation_df = target_allocations,
#'   alloc_size_var = "sample_size",
#'   seed = 123
#' )
#' }
draw_strs_sample <- function(
    data,
    county_var = "county",
    allocation_df,
    alloc_size_var = "sample",
    seed = as.numeric(Sys.Date())
){

  set.seed(seed)

  joined_frame <- data %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      allocation_df,
      by = county_var
    )

  joined_frame %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(county_var))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::slice_sample(
      n = min(dplyr::n(), first(.data[[alloc_size_var]]))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}
```


## two stage cluster random sampling

```{r function-draw_cluster_sample}
#' Draw a Two-Stage Cluster Sample of Households
#'
#' This function performs two-stage cluster sampling within counties. In the 
#' first stage, a specified number of unique villages are selected randomly. In the 
#' second stage, a fixed number of households are randomly drawn from each 
#' of those selected villages. Both target sizes are pulled from the allocation frame.
#'
#' @param data A data frame containing raw household-level records.
#' @param county_var The bare or quoted column name identifying the county stratum.
#' @param village_id_var The bare or quoted column name identifying the unique village.
#' @param allocation_df A data frame containing columns for the county identifier, 
#'   the target village sample size, and the target household sample size per village.
#' @param alloc_villages_var The bare or quoted column name in `allocation_df` 
#'   indicating the number of villages to sample per county.
#' @param alloc_hh_var The bare or quoted column name in `allocation_df` 
#'   indicating the number of households to sample per chosen village.
#' @param seed An integer value used to initialize the pseudo-random number generator 
#'   for reproducible sampling. Defaults to `42`.
#'
#' @return A data frame containing the cluster-sampled household rows.
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr group_by mutate ungroup arrange row_number filter across any_of distinct n inner_join select
#' @importFrom rlang sym
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # dummy raw household data
#' raw_households <- data.frame(
#'   county_id = rep(c("County_A", "County_B"), each = 15),
#'   village_id = c(rep("V1", 5), rep("V2", 5), rep("V3", 5), 
#'                  rep("V4", 5), rep("V5", 5), rep("V6", 5)),
#'   household_id = paste0("HH_", 1:30)
#' )
#'
#' # multi-stage target allocations dataframe
#' cluster_allocations <- data.frame(
#'   county_id = c("County_A", "County_B"),
#'   target_villages = c(2, 2),
#'   target_hh_per_village = c(3, 2)
#' )
#'
#' # run dynamic cluster sampling
#' cluster_sample <- draw_cluster_sample(
#'   data = raw_households,
#'   county_var = "county_id",
#'   village_id_var = "village_id",
#'   allocation_df = cluster_allocations,
#'   alloc_villages_var = "target_villages",
#'   alloc_hh_var = "target_hh_per_village",
#'   seed = 42
#' )
#' }
draw_cluster_sample <- function(
    data,
    county_var = "county",
    village_id_var = "village",
    allocation_df,
    alloc_villages_var = "target_villages",
    alloc_hh_var = "target_hh_per_village",
    seed = 42
){

  set.seed(seed)

  selected_villages <- data %>%
    dplyr::distinct(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(
          c(county_var, village_id_var)
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      allocation_df,
      by = county_var
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(county_var)
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::slice_sample(
      n = min(
        dplyr::n(),
        first(.data[[alloc_villages_var]])
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  data %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      selected_villages,
      by = c(county_var, village_id_var)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(
          c(county_var, village_id_var)
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::slice_sample(
      n = min(
        dplyr::n(),
        first(.data[[alloc_hh_var]])
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}
```

## systematic sampling county level

```{r function-draw_systematic_across_villages}
#' Draw a Systematic Sample of Households Spreading Across Villages
#'
#' This function selects a systematic random sample of individual household rows 
#' from within counties. By sorting by village first, the systematic interval 
#' automatically spreads the selected sample evenly across the different villages.
#'
#' @param data A data frame containing raw household-level records.
#' @param county_var The bare or quoted column name identifying the county stratum.
#' @param village_id_var The bare or quoted column name identifying the unique village.
#' @param allocation_df A data frame containing two columns: the county identifier 
#'   and the allocated household sample size for that county.
#' @param alloc_size_var The bare or quoted column name in `allocation_df` 
#'   indicating the target sample size.
#' @param seed An integer value used to initialize the pseudo-random number generator. 
#'   Defaults to `42`.
#'
#' @return A data frame containing the systematically selected household rows.
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr group_by mutate ungroup inner_join arrange row_number filter across any_of n select
#' @importFrom rlang sym
#' @export
draw_systematic_across_villages <- function(
    data,
    county_var = "county",
    village_id_var = "village",
    allocation_df,
    alloc_size_var = "sample",
    seed = as.numeric(Sys.Date())
){

  set.seed(seed)

  joined_frame <- data %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      allocation_df,
      by = county_var
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(
          c(county_var, village_id_var)
        )
      )
    )

  joined_frame %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(county_var)
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(~{

      df <- .x

      N <- nrow(df)
      n_target <- min(
        first(df[[alloc_size_var]]),
        N
      )

      k <- N / n_target

      start <- sample(
        seq_len(ceiling(k)),
        1
      )

      idx <- floor(
        start + (0:(n_target-1))*k
      )

      idx <- pmin(idx, N)

      df[idx, , drop = FALSE]

    }) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}
```

## create survey object

```{r function-create_survey_object}
#' create a survey design object dynamically for any complex sampling design
#'
#' @param sample_df dataframe containing the final selected sample observations
#' @param population_df dataframe containing the full original population sampling frame
#' @param id_cols character vector identifying structural cluster nodes in cascading order (e.g., c("village", "hh_id"))
#' @param strata_cols character vector containing names of stratification columns (optional, defaults to NULL)
#' @param weight_col_name character string naming the output column for calculated weights
#'
#' @returns a configured survey design object
#' @export
create_survey_object <- function(sample_df, 
                                        population_df, 
                                        id_cols, 
                                        strata_cols = NULL, 
                                        weight_col_name = "sampling_weight") {
  
  # ensure package namespace dependencies are available
  if (!base::requireNamespace("survey", quietly = TRUE)) {
    base::stop("the 'survey' package is required but not installed")
  }
  
  # handle missing variable safety up front
  all_vars <- base::unique(c(id_cols, strata_cols))
  missing_sample <- all_vars[!all_vars %in% base::names(sample_df)]
  missing_pop    <- all_vars[!all_vars %in% base::names(population_df)]
  
  if (base::length(missing_sample) > 0 || base::length(missing_pop) > 0) {
    base::stop("specified structural columns missing from sample or population dataframes")
  }
  
  # step 1: isolate stage 1 units (primary sampling units) to evaluate selection probabilities
  psu_col <- id_cols[1]
  stage1_grouping <- base::unique(c(strata_cols, psu_col))
  
  pop_psus <- population_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(stage1_grouping))) %>%
    dplyr::count(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(strata_cols)), name = "..total_PSUs_in_strata..")
  
  sample_psus <- sample_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(stage1_grouping))) %>%
    dplyr::count(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(strata_cols)), name = "..sampled_PSUs_in_strata..")
  
  # map stage 1 probability across rows
  stage1_probs <- population_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(stage1_grouping))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(pop_psus, by = strata_cols) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sample_psus, by = strata_cols) %>%
    # if unstratified, handle empty grouping count variables safely
    dplyr::mutate(
      ..total_PSUs_in_strata..   = base::ifelse(base::is.na(..total_PSUs_in_strata..), base::length(base::unique(population_df[[psu_col]])), ..total_PSUs_in_strata..),
      ..sampled_PSUs_in_strata.. = base::ifelse(base::is.na(..sampled_PSUs_in_strata..), base::length(base::unique(sample_df[[psu_col]])), ..sampled_PSUs_in_strata..),
      ..prob_stage1..            = ..sampled_PSUs_in_strata.. / ..total_PSUs_in_strata..
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(stage1_grouping), "..prob_stage1..")
  
  # step 2: evaluate stage 2 units (secondary sampling units) if a second id column is specified
  if (base::length(id_cols) > 1) {
    ssu_grouping <- base::unique(c(strata_cols, id_cols[1:2]))
    
    pop_ssus <- population_df %>%
      dplyr::count(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(id_cols[1])), name = "..total_SSUs_in_PSU..")
    
    sample_ssus <- sample_df %>%
      dplyr::count(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(id_cols[1])), name = "..sampled_SSUs_in_PSU..")
    
    stage2_probs <- pop_ssus %>%
      dplyr::left_join(sample_ssus, by = id_cols[1]) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        ..sampled_SSUs_in_PSU.. = base::ifelse(base::is.na(..sampled_SSUs_in_PSU..), 0, ..sampled_SSUs_in_PSU..),
        ..prob_stage2..         = ..sampled_SSUs_in_PSU.. / ..total_SSUs_in_PSU..
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(id_cols[1]), "..prob_stage2..")
    
    # join stage 1 and stage 2 tracks together to compute joint weights
    final_weights <- stage1_probs %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(stage2_probs, by = id_cols[1]) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!weight_col_name := 1 / (..prob_stage1.. * ..prob_stage2..)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(id_cols[1], weight_col_name)))
    
  } else {
    # single stage designs pass flat inverse probability configurations down stream
    final_weights <- stage1_probs %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!weight_col_name := 1 / ..prob_stage1..
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(stage1_grouping, weight_col_name)))
  }
  
  # step 3: combine finalized weights lookup to sample frame and create svydesign object
  sample_with_weights <- sample_df %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(final_weights, by = id_cols[1])
  
  id_formula     <- stats::as.formula(base::paste0("~", base::paste(id_cols, collapse = " + ")))
  strata_formula <- if (!base::is.null(strata_cols)) stats::as.formula(base::paste0("~", base::paste(strata_cols, collapse = " + "))) else NULL
  weight_formula <- stats::as.formula(base::paste0("~", weight_col_name))
  
  survey_obj <- survey::svydesign(
    ids = id_formula,
    strata = strata_formula,
    weights = weight_formula,
    data = sample_with_weights
  )
  
  return(survey_obj)
}
```


## apply corrections

```{r function-apply_corrections}
#' Apply Data Cleaning Corrections Using an Embedded Cleaning Log
#'
#' This function updates a main dataset using a correction data frame. It applies
#' standard cell corrections and handles row deletions last. Deletions are processed 
#' using strict unique UUID matching if a true uuid column is present, falling back to 
#' exact name matching combined with multiple context validation columns if a general 
#' non-unique identifier or name-only tracking is used.
#'
#' @param data A data frame containing the main dataset to be cleaned.
#' @param id_var The bare or quoted column name representing the unique identifier.
#' @param corrections A data frame containing the corrections log along with the matching keys.
#' @param var_to_change_col Column name in `corrections` holding target names to change.
#' @param correct_value_col Column name in `corrections` holding updated values.
#' @param ben_name_col Column name in both datasets holding beneficiary names.
#' @param context_cols Optional character vector. Secondary column names present in both 
#'   datasets (e.g., `c("ben_id_number", "ward", "village")`) used to build a composite key 
#'   and avoid accidental collisions of identical or similar names.
#'
#' @return A data frame matching the structure of `data`.
#' @export
apply_corrections <- function(
    data, 
    id_var = "uuid", 
    corrections, 
    var_to_change_col = "var_to_change", 
    correct_value_col = "correct_value",
    ben_name_col = "ben_name",
    context_cols = c("ben_id_number", "ward", "village")
) {
  
  id_str <- as.character(substitute(id_var))
  if (!id_str %in% names(data)) id_str <- id_var
  
  var_change_str <- as.character(substitute(var_to_change_col))
  if (!var_change_str %in% names(corrections)) var_change_str <- var_to_change_col
  
  correct_val_str <- as.character(substitute(correct_value_col))
  if (!correct_val_str %in% names(corrections)) correct_val_str <- correct_value_col
  
  ben_name_str <- as.character(substitute(ben_name_col))
  if (!ben_name_str %in% names(corrections)) ben_name_str <- ben_name_col
  
  cleaned_data <- data
  
  # extract only the unique variables that actually exist in the main data
  distinct_vars <- corrections %>%
    dplyr::filter(!!rlang::sym(var_change_str) %in% names(cleaned_data)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(!!rlang::sym(var_change_str)) %>%
    unique()
  
  # 1 execute standard cell corrections first
  for (current_var in distinct_vars) {
    sub_corrections <- corrections %>%
      dplyr::filter(!!rlang::sym(var_change_str) == current_var) %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(ben_name_str, correct_val_str)))
    
    target_class <- class(cleaned_data[[current_var]])[1]
    
    if (target_class %in% c("numeric", "integer")) {
      sub_corrections[[correct_val_str]] <- as.numeric(sub_corrections[[correct_val_str]])
    } else if (target_class == "logical") {
      sub_corrections[[correct_val_str]] <- as.logical(sub_corrections[[correct_val_str]])
    } else {
      sub_corrections[[correct_val_str]] <- as.character(sub_corrections[[correct_val_str]])
    }
    
    join_target_name <- paste0("new_val_", current_var)
    sub_corrections <- dplyr::rename(
      sub_corrections, 
      !!rlang::sym(join_target_name) := !!rlang::sym(correct_val_str)
    )
    
    cleaned_data <- cleaned_data %>%
      dplyr::left_join(sub_corrections, by = ben_name_str) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!rlang::sym(current_var) := ifelse(
          !is.na(!!rlang::sym(join_target_name)), 
          !!rlang::sym(join_target_name), 
          !!rlang::sym(current_var)
        )
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(join_target_name))
  }
  
  # 2 handle deletions as the final operation with compound keys
  if (var_change_str %in% names(corrections) && ben_name_str %in% names(corrections) && ben_name_str %in% names(data)) {
    
    # filter log down strictly to the rows designated for deletion using case insensitive grepl
    delete_log <- corrections %>%
      dplyr::filter(grepl("delete", !!rlang::sym(var_change_str), ignore.case = TRUE))
    
    if (nrow(delete_log) > 0) {
      
      # premium bypass: only use direct ID deletion if it is explicitly a unique uuid column
      if (tolower(id_str) == "uuid" && id_str %in% names(corrections) && id_str %in% names(data)) {
        
        delete_ids <- delete_log %>%
          dplyr::pull(!!rlang::sym(id_str)) %>%
          unique()
        
        cleaned_data <- cleaned_data %>%
          dplyr::filter(!(!!rlang::sym(id_str) %in% delete_ids))
        
      } else {
        # traditional fallback: filter context columns down to only those that actually exist in both datasets
        # this ensures that if id_str is "ben_id_number", it gets lumped safely into the compound validation checks
        all_potential_contexts <- unique(c(id_str, context_cols))
        valid_contexts <- all_potential_contexts[all_potential_contexts %in% names(data) & all_potential_contexts %in% names(corrections)]
        
        if (length(valid_contexts) > 0) {
          # combine beneficiary name and all valid context values into a multi-variable string key
          # using individual rowwise evaluations to avoid vector collapse traps
          build_composite_key <- function(df, name_col, ctx_cols) {
            df %>%
              dplyr::rowwise() %>%
              dplyr::mutate(
                comp_key = paste(
                  c(as.character(.data[[name_col]]), mget(ctx_cols)), 
                  collapse = "|||"
                )
              ) %>%
              dplyr::ungroup() %>%
              dplyr::pull(comp_key)
          }
          
          # generate keys for both datasets
          delete_keys <- build_composite_key(delete_log, ben_name_str, valid_contexts)
          
          # apply filter by checking the main data against the delete keys
          cleaned_data <- cleaned_data %>%
            dplyr::rowwise() %>%
            dplyr::filter(
              !paste(c(as.character(.data[[ben_name_str]]), mget(valid_contexts)), collapse = "|||") %in% delete_keys
            ) %>%
            dplyr::ungroup()
          
        } else {
          # fallback to strict exact name checking if no valid context variables were matched
          delete_names <- unique(delete_log[[ben_name_str]])
          cleaned_data <- cleaned_data %>%
            dplyr::filter(!(!!rlang::sym(ben_name_str) %in% delete_names))
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(cleaned_data)
}

```

## read excel workbook

```{r function-read_workbook}
#' Read Excel sheets or an entire workbook into a list or data frame with clean names
#'
#' @description
#' Iterates through available worksheets within an Excel file or targets a specific sheet, 
#' extracts content while skipping a designated number of rows, and standardizes column names 
#' using snake_case. If the target evaluation resolves to exactly one worksheet, it automatically 
#' drops the list format and returns a single data frame directly.
#'
#' @param path Character string representing the path to the Excel file.
#' @param bind_rows Logical indicator. If TRUE, binds multiple extracted sheets into 
#'   a single unified data frame using a compiler identifier column. Defaults to FALSE.
#' @param id Character string naming the optional identifier column that tracks 
#'   the source sheet name when `bind_rows` is TRUE. Defaults to "sheet_name".
#' @param skip Integer specifying the number of rows to skip at the start of reading. Defaults to 0.
#' @param sheet_name Character string specifying a single sheet to read. If NULL, all sheets are processed. Defaults to NULL.
#'
#' @return A single data frame if only one sheet is processed or `bind_rows = TRUE`. 
#'   Otherwise, a named list of data frames representing individual sheets.
#'
#' @importFrom readxl excel_sheets read_excel
#' @importFrom purrr set_names map list_rbind
#' @importFrom janitor clean_names
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # read a specific sheet and skip the first 2 rows
#' df_raw <- read_workbook("survey_data.xlsx", sheet_name = "Main_Data", skip = 2)
#' }
read_workbook <- function(path, bind_rows = FALSE, id = "sheet_name", skip = 0, sheet_name = NULL) {
  
  # determine target sheet names based on user input selection
  if (!is.null(sheet_name)) {
    sheet_names <- sheet_name
  } else {
    sheet_names <- readxl::excel_sheets(path)
  }
  
  # short circuit and return a single data frame instantly if only one sheet is target evaluated
  if (length(sheet_names) == 1) {
    single_df <- readxl::read_excel(path = path, sheet = sheet_names, skip = skip) %>%
      janitor::clean_names()
    return(single_df)
  }
  
  # extract sheet names, read contents, and standardize variables to snake case
  sheets_list <- sheet_names %>%
    purrr::set_names() %>%
    purrr::map(~ {
      readxl::read_excel(path = path, sheet = .x, skip = skip) %>%
        janitor::clean_names()
    })
  
  # conditionally collapse the list rows into a single data frame if specified
  if (bind_rows) {
    combined_data <- purrr::list_rbind(sheets_list, names_to = id)
    return(combined_data)
  }
  
  return(sheets_list)
}
```


## standardize names

```{r function-standardize_names}
#' Map and Standardize Administrative Names to Reference Values
#'
#' This function takes a dataset containing entered administrative names (such as
#' sublocations or villages) and cross-references them against an official lookup
#' table. It matches names using an optimal string alignment distance algorithm
#' to automatically correct typos, casing differences, and minor variations.
#'
#' @param data A data frame containing the main survey or household records.
#' @param match_col A bare or quoted column name in \code{data} containing the 
#'   entered names that need correction.
#' @param ref_df A data frame serving as the official reference lookup table.
#' @param ref_col A bare or quoted column name in \code{ref_df} containing the
#'   true, standardized reference names.
#' @param max_dist A numeric value specifying the maximum allowed string distance
#'   for a match to be considered valid. Greater values allow more generous 
#'   typo corrections. Defaults to \code{2}.
#'
#' @return A data frame with the same rows as \code{data}, where the original
#'   \code{match_col} values are replaced by the true values from \code{ref_col}.
#'   Unmatched records will retain their original values or return \code{NA} if 
#'   completely outside the distance threshold.
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate row_number across any_of
#' @importFrom rlang .data
#' @importFrom stringdist amatch
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # dummy raw survey data with typos
#' survey_records <- data.frame(
#'   household_id = 1:4,
#'   entered_sublocation = c("Muguga ", "Kikuyu", "sigona", "UnknownPlace")
#' )
#'
#' # true official reference registry
#' official_sublocations <- data.frame(
#'   true_name = c("Muguga", "Kikuyu", "Sigona", "Karai")
#' )
#'
#' # clean and standardize the sublocation entries
#' cleaned_data <- standardize_names(
#'   data      = survey_records,
#'   match_col = "entered_sublocation",
#'   ref_df    = official_sublocations,
#'   ref_col   = "true_name",
#'   max_dist  = 3
#' )
#' }
standardize_names <- function(
    data,
    match_col,
    ref_df,
    ref_col,
    max_dist = 2
) {
  
  # convert input column names safely to standard strings
  match_str <- as.character(substitute(match_col))
  if (!match_str %in% names(data)) match_str <- match_col
  
  ref_str <- as.character(substitute(ref_col))
  if (!ref_str %in% names(ref_df)) ref_str <- ref_col
  
  # extract the target reference vector clean of missing entries
  ref_vector <- as.character(na.omit(ref_df[[ref_str]]))
  
  # extract and clean input entries for robust string matching
  raw_entries <- as.character(data[[match_str]])
  clean_raw   <- trimws(tolower(raw_entries))
  clean_ref   <- trimws(tolower(ref_vector))
  
  # find matching vector indices based on optimal string alignment distance
  match_indices <- stringdist::amatch(
    x          = clean_raw,
    table      = clean_ref,
    method     = "osa",
    maxDist    = max_dist
  )
  
  # map matched indices back to original true casing from reference list
  standardized_values <- ifelse(
    !is.na(match_indices),
    ref_vector[match_indices],
    raw_entries
  )
  
  # assign corrected values back to the original target column mask
  standardized_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::any_of(match_str),
        ~ standardized_values
      )
    )
  
  return(standardized_df)
}
```


## find name matches

```{r function-find_name_matches}
#' Identify Potential Beneficiary Name Matches From a Master Dataset
#'
#' @description
#' Compares a column of names in a flagged dataset against a column of names in a 
#' master reference dataset using optimized vectorized string distance matrices. 
#' If a potential match is identified within a specified text edit threshold, 
#' the candidate name from the master dataset is mapped into a new column named `name_possible`.
#'
#' @param flagged_data A data frame containing the flagged records needing verification.
#' @param master_data A data frame containing the verified master benchmark records.
#' @param flagged_col The bare or quoted column name of the name column in `flagged_data`. Defaults to "ben_name".
#' @param master_col The bare or quoted column name of the name column in `master_data`. Defaults to "ben_name".
#' @param max_dist Integer specifying the maximum allowed string distance/edits to qualify as a match. Defaults to 3.
#'
#' @return A data frame matching the structure of `flagged_data`, with an additional 
#'   `name_possible` character column containing the matched master dataset name (or NA if no match is found).
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate left_join select any_of tibble
#' @importFrom utils adist
#' @importFrom rlang sym !! :=
#' @importFrom stringdist stringdistmatrix
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' verified_df <- find_name_matches(bad_data, good_data, max_dist = 2)
#' }


find_name_matches <- function(
    flagged_data,
    master_data,
    flagged_col = "ben_name",
    master_col  = "ben_name",
    max_dist    = 3
) {
  flag_str <- as.character(substitute(flagged_col))
  if (!flag_str %in% names(flagged_data)) flag_str <- flagged_col
  
  master_str <- as.character(substitute(master_col))
  if (!master_str %in% names(master_data)) master_str <- master_col
  
  master_pool <- unique(na.omit(as.character(master_data[[master_str]])))
  flagged_vec <- as.character(flagged_data[[flag_str]])
  
  sort_tokens <- function(x) {
    vapply(
      strsplit(tolower(trimws(x)), "[[:space:]\\-]+"),
      function(toks) paste(sort(toks), collapse = " "),
      character(1)
    )
  }
  
  flagged_lower <- tolower(flagged_vec)
  master_lower  <- tolower(master_pool)
  flagged_tok   <- sort_tokens(flagged_vec)
  master_tok    <- sort_tokens(master_pool)
  
  # blocking key: first character of the first token
  flagged_block <- substr(flagged_tok, 1, 1)
  master_block  <- substr(master_tok,  1, 1)
  
  name_possible <- rep(NA_character_, length(flagged_vec))
  
  for (block in unique(flagged_block)) {
    fi <- which(flagged_block == block)   # row indices in flagged
    mi <- which(master_block  == block)   # candidate indices in master
    
    if (length(fi) == 0 || length(mi) == 0) next
    
    dist_whole <- stringdist::stringdistmatrix(
      flagged_lower[fi], master_lower[mi],
      method = "osa", nthread = parallel::detectCores()
    )
    dist_token <- stringdist::stringdistmatrix(
      flagged_tok[fi], master_tok[mi],
      method = "osa", nthread = parallel::detectCores()
    )
    dist_best <- pmin(dist_whole, dist_token)
    
    best_col  <- max.col(-dist_best, ties.method = "first")
    best_dist <- dist_best[cbind(seq_along(fi), best_col)]
    
    matched <- best_dist <= max_dist
    name_possible[fi[matched]] <- master_pool[mi[best_col[matched]]]
  }
  
  flagged_data[["name_possible"]] <- name_possible
  flagged_data
}

```


## match county records

```{r function-match_county_records}
#' Filter and Match Payroll Records Against Registration Data by County
#'
#' @description
#' Subsets registration data for a specific county, removes duplicate IDs,
#' joins the results with payroll records, and flags rows where the payroll name
#' is a partial match inside the registration name string.
#'
#' @param registration A data frame containing the primary registration benchmark records.
#' @param payroll A data frame containing the target payroll records to verify.
#' @param county_name Character string specifying the county name to filter on. Defaults to "Tana".
#'
#' @return A data frame matching the layout of the payroll dataset, appended with 
#'   columns from the subsetted registration data and a logical `names_match` flag.
#'
#' @importFrom dplyr filter select distinct left_join mutate
#' @importFrom stringi stri_detect_fixed
#'
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{match_county_records()}
match_county_records <- function(registration, payroll, county_name = "Tana") {
  # filter registration pool for the target county and drop duplicate id records
  df_county_ref <- registration %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl(county_name, county, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::select(ben_name, reg_num, ben_id_number) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(ben_id_number, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  # merge payroll records with the clean county reference subset
  df_joined <- payroll %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      df_county_ref,
      by = c("id_number" = "ben_id_number")
    ) %>%
    # remove residual system export columns starting with x or X
    dplyr::select(-grep("^[xX]", names(.)))
  
  # fast vectorized string detection — no r loops or nested scans
  df_joined %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      names_match = !is.na(name_payroll) & 
        !is.na(ben_name) & 
        name_payroll != "" & 
        stringi::stri_detect_fixed(ben_name, name_payroll, case_insensitive = TRUE)
    )
}
```


## normalize names

```{r function-normalize_names}
#' Normalize a Name Vector
#'
#' @description
#' Cleans a character vector of names by collapsing extra whitespace,
#' trimming leading/trailing spaces, and converting to title case.
#'
#' @param x A character vector of names.
#'
#' @return A cleaned character vector.
#'
#' @importFrom stringr str_squish str_to_title
#'
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{normalize_names()}
normalize_names <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_squish(x)       # trims + collapses internal spaces
  x <- stringr::str_to_title(x)     # title case
  x
}
```

## Veification criteria table

```{r function-gen_verification_criteria_table}
#' Create the target beneficiary verification criteria and indicators summary
#'
#' @description
#' Builds a two column matrix pairing each humanitarian vulnerability 
#' criterion alongside its designated operational indicator visually 
#' merging repeating criteria rows and introducing complete outer frame grids 
#' that fully enclose column headers with explicit bold top and bottom lines
#'
#' @param df dataframe of verification criteria
#' @param title character vector of title
#' @return A styled flextable object containing the merged two column layout with 
#' fully enclosed bold grid line formatting
#'
#' @importFrom tibble tibble
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate lag
#' @importFrom flextable flextable as_paragraph as_chunk align valign width border_outer border_inner_h border_inner_v bg color bold font set_caption delete_part add_footer_lines
#' @importFrom officer fp_border fp_text
#'
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{gen_verification_criteria_table()}
gen_verification_criteria_table <- function(
    df = verification_criteria,
    title = "Vulnerability Criteria"
    ) {
  
  # track total row count
  total_rows <- nrow(df)
  
  # track the indices where a new criteria block begins for main horizontal lines
  main_grid_rows <- c(7, 12, 15, 16)
  
  # define the explicit border properties using officer
  heavy_border <- officer::fp_border(color = "#0B1054", width = 2.5, style = "solid")
  mid_border   <- officer::fp_border(color = "#0B1054", width = 2, style = "solid")
  thin_border  <- officer::fp_border(color = "#d3d3d3", width = 1, style = "solid")
  
  # build the flextable layout structure
  styled_table <- flextable::flextable(df) %>%
    # visually merge repeating cell items sequentially along the vertical axis
    flextable::merge_v(j = ~ Criteria) %>%
    # map alignments and set relative layout sizing to fit standard pages
    flextable::align(align = "left", part = "all") %>%
    flextable::valign(valign = "top", part = "body") %>%
    flextable::width(j = "Criteria", width = 2.2) %>%
    flextable::width(j = "Indicator", width = 4.3) %>%
    
    # apply deep blue background fill with white bold text for column labels
    flextable::bg(bg = "#0B1054", part = "header") %>%
    flextable::color(color = "white", part = "header") %>%
    flextable::bold(part = "header") %>%
    
    # apply a standard baseline horizontal grid line separating every single indicator row
    flextable::border_inner_h(border = thin_border, part = "body") %>%
    
    # overlay bold main horizontal block dividers within the body row structures
    flextable::hline(i = (main_grid_rows - 1), border = mid_border, part = "body") %>%
    
    # construct complete outer frame borders and center divider line enclosing headers and rows
    flextable::border_outer(border = heavy_border, part = "all") %>%
    flextable::border_inner_v(border = mid_border, part = "all") %>%
    
    # add font settings and map the source footnote notes cleanly to the bottom layout
    flextable::font(fontname = "Arial", part = "all") %>%
    flextable::add_footer_lines(
      values = "Acronym Definitions: OTP - Outpatient Therapeutic Program; SFP - Supplementary Feeding Program; FCS - Food Consumption Score; HHs - Households"
    ) %>%
    flextable::font(fontname = "Arial", part = "footer")
  
  return(styled_table)
}
```

```{r function-get_vulnerability_data}
#' get vulnerability criteria (physiological, nutritional etc)

#' \dontrun{get_vulnerability_data()}
get_vulnerability_data <- function(){

    select(type, name, label, n) %>%
```

## automate indicators

```{r function-automate_indicators}
#' Automate binary indicator variable creation
#'
#' This function dynamically scans input columns, handles missing data structures,
#' cleans raw count variables, and generates binary 0/1 indicators based on 
#' underlying numeric and character type properties, preserving the original name.
#'
#' @param df A dataframe or tibble object.
#' @param cols A character vector specifying the target column names to process.
#'
#' @return A modified dataframe with updated raw counts and appended indicator columns.
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate across all_of if_else
#' @importFrom stringr str_detect
#' @export
automate_indicators <- function(df, cols) {
  df %>%
    # first pass clean all raw numeric count inputs to handle nas and zeros universally
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(cols),
        function(x) {
          # lower case comments without dots or dashes
          if (is.numeric(x)) {
            return(dplyr::if_else(is.na(x) | x == 0, 0, x))
          }
          return(x)
        }
      )
    ) %>%
    # second pass generate indicators and append ind cleanly to the original column names
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(cols), 
        function(x) {
          if (is.numeric(x)) {
            indicator <- dplyr::if_else(x == 0, 0, 1)
            return(indicator)
          } 
          
          # explicitly separate affirmative responses from negative or uncertain ones
          clean_x <- tolower(x)
          indicator <- dplyr::if_else(
            is.na(x) | 
              clean_x == "no" | 
              stringr::str_detect(clean_x, "not_at_all|not_really|dont_know|don't know"), 
            0, 
            1
          )
          return(indicator)
        }, 
        .names = "{.col}_ind"
      )
    )
}
```

## donut plot

```{r function-plot_parts_donut}
#' visualize parts to whole using a donut layout framework
#'
#' @param data dataframe
#' @param fill_col character. the categorical column to slice
#' @param palette character vector. hex color values
#'
#' @returns a ggplot object
#' @importFrom dplyr count mutate across all_of
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_col geom_text scale_fill_manual theme_void theme coord_polar xlim position_stack
#' @importFrom scales percent
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{plot_parts_donut()}
plot_parts_donut <- function(data, fill_col, palette = c("#81C784", "#FFB74D", "#E65100")) {
  
  # lower case comments without dots or dashes
  # map labels and compute dynamic cumulative coordinates for clean radial centering
  plot_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(fill_col))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      pct = n / sum(n),
      pct_label = paste0(
        # .data[[fill_col]], 
        # "\n(", 
        scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1)
        # ,")"
      )
    )
  
  ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = 3, y = pct, fill = .data[[fill_col]])) +
    # maintain stable donut ring layout thickness
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = 1, color = "white", size = 0.5) +
    # shift text position horizontally outward beyond the main donut frame
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(x = 4.2, label = pct_label),
      position = ggplot2::position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
      color = "black",
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = palette) +
    ggplot2::coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    # expand the coordinate map boundary to give labels complete breathing room
    ggplot2::xlim(c(1, 5.2)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}
```

## faceted donuts

```{r function-plot_faceted_donuts}
#' visualize parts to whole using an automated faceted donut grid via patchwork
#'
#' @param data dataframe
#' @param fill_col character the categorical variable to slice 
#' @param facet_col character the variable to split panels by 
#' @param palette character vector hex color values mapping to categories
#'
#' @returns a patchwork grid assembly of donut plots
#' @importFrom dplyr filter count mutate pull
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_col geom_text scale_fill_manual theme_void theme coord_polar xlim labs element_text position_stack
#' @importFrom patchwork wrap_plots plot_layout
#' @importFrom stringr str_to_title
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{plot_faceted_donuts()}
plot_faceted_donuts <- function(data, 
                                fill_col, 
                                facet_col, 
                                palette = c("#388E3C", "#F57C00", "#D32F2F")) {
  
  # extract unique facet groups while ignoring missing rows
  facet_groups <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[facet_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::pull(.data[[facet_col]]) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort()
  
  # dynamically determine optimal column layouts based on category lengths
  n_facets <- length(facet_groups)
  calculated_ncol <- if (n_facets <= 3) {
    n_facets
  } else if (n_facets == 4) {
    2
  } else {
    3
  }
  
  # generate individual donut objects iteratively
  plot_list <- lapply(facet_groups, function(group) {
    
    # filter down to single panel subset
    sub_df <- data %>% 
      dplyr::filter(.data[[facet_col]] == group, !is.na(.data[[fill_col]]))
    
    # safeguard against empty group metrics
    if (nrow(sub_df) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    plot_df <- sub_df %>%
      dplyr::count(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(fill_col))) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        pct = n / sum(n),
        pct_label = paste0(
          scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1)
        )
      )
    
    ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = 3, y = pct, fill = .data[[fill_col]])) +
      # maintain donut thickness between inner and outer radius limits
      ggplot2::geom_col(width = 1, color = "white", size = 0.5) +
      # push text radius position out beyond the chart area boundary
      ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(x = 4.2, label = pct_label),
        position = ggplot2::position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
        color = "black",
        fontface = "bold",
        size = 2.8
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = palette) +
      ggplot2::coord_polar(theta = "y") +
      # expand structural coordinate canvas limits to prevent text clipping
      ggplot2::xlim(c(1, 5.2)) +
      ggplot2::labs(title = stringr::str_to_title(group)) +
      ggplot2::theme_void() +
      ggplot2::theme(
        # removed legend position here to let patchwork handle it
        plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 11, vjust = -1)
      )
  })
  
  # drop null items from tracking list
  # using base r filter option to keep namespaces minimal
  plot_list <- plot_list[!sapply(plot_list, is.null)]
  
  # stitch panels together and collect legends into a single unified guide
  combined_grid <- patchwork::wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = calculated_ncol) +
    patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  return(combined_grid)
}
```

## theme plots

```{r function-theme_plots}
#' publication ready theme wrapper using cowplot with gridlines

#' @param base_size numeric base font size

#'
#' @returns a ggplot2 theme object
#' @importFrom cowplot theme_minimal_grid

theme_plots <- function(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") {

        hjust = 0.5,
        color = "grey30",
        face = "plain",
        margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 8)
      ),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}
```

## save plots as .png

```{r function-save_plots_to_png}
#' save a list of active plots into a grid using the png device
#'
#' @param plot_list list of ggplot or grid objects
#' @param output_path character path where the combined grid will be saved
#' @param ncol integer number of columns in the grid
#' @param width integer width of output image in pixels
#' @param height integer height of output image in pixels
#' @param res integer nominal resolution in ppi
#'
#' @return invisible null saves file directly to disk
#' @importFrom grDevices png dev.off
#' @importFrom grid grid.newpage pushViewport viewport grid.layout
#' @export
save_plots_to_png <- function(plot_list, 
                                   output_path, 
                                   ncol = 2, 
                                   width = 1600, 
                                   height = 1200, 
                                   res = 144) {
  
  # calculate layout grid dimensions based on total plot count
  n_plots <- length(plot_list)
  nrow <- ceiling(n_plots / ncol)
  
  # open the native png graphics device to catch the upcoming draw calls
  grDevices::png(
    filename = output_path, 
    width = width, 
    height = height, 
    res = res
  )
  
  # initialize a fresh blank grid canvas page
  grid::grid.newpage()
  
  # push the base grid layout matrix structure onto the canvas
  grid::pushViewport(
    grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(nrow, ncol))
  )
  
  # loop through every plot object in the list and assign coordinates
  for (i in seq_along(plot_list)) {
    row_idx <- ceiling(i / ncol)
    col_idx <- (i - 1) %% ncol + 1
    
    # render the plot directly into its designated grid cell coordinates
    print(
      plot_list[[i]], 
      vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = row_idx, layout.pos.col = col_idx)
    )
  }
  
  # shut down the active device to commit and write the file to disk
  grDevices::dev.off()
}
```


## plot household counts

```{r function-plot_household_counts}
#' plot household aggregation counts using unicode location pins with bold plotmath ggrepel label text callouts
#'
#' @param data dataframe containing household level records
#' @param lat_col character name of the latitude column
#' @param lon_col character name of the longitude column
#' @param group_by character administrative grouping scale choice, either 'ward' or 'county'
#' @param compass_pos character layout position for the north arrow, defaults to 'bl'
#' @param font_size numeric. font size for labels
#'
#' @returns a ggplot object
#' @importFrom dplyr filter group_by summarise n count left_join mutate
#' @importFrom sf st_as_sf st_join st_centroid st_coordinates st_drop_geometry
#' @importFrom geodata gadm
#' @importFrom ggspatial annotation_north_arrow north_arrow_minimal
#' @importFrom ggrepel geom_text_repel
#' @importFrom grid arrow unit
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot geom_sf geom_text aes labs theme_minimal theme element_text coord_sf element_rect
#' @export
plot_household_counts <- function(data, lat_col, lon_col, group_by = "ward", compass_pos = "bl", font_size = 2.8) {
  
  # isolate coordinates and filter out missing records
  plot_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[lat_col]]), !is.na(.data[[lon_col]]))
  
  # transform the raw dataframe into a coordinate spatial sf object (wgs84 projection)
  sf_df <- sf::st_as_sf(
    plot_df, 
    coords = c(lon_col, lat_col), 
    crs = 4326
  )
  
  # dynamically download the official boundaries from gadm database
  kenya_spatvector_l1 <- geodata::gadm(country = "KEN", level = 1, path = base::tempdir())
  kenya_counties_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(kenya_spatvector_l1)
  
  kenya_spatvector_l3 <- geodata::gadm(country = "KEN", level = 3, path = base::tempdir())
  kenya_wards_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(kenya_spatvector_l3)
  
  # aggregate counts and build mathematical bold display labels based on chosen administrative group scale
  if (group_by == "ward") {
    # spatially join household coordinates to identify active ward parents
    sf_joined <- suppressMessages(sf::st_join(sf_df, kenya_wards_sf, join = sf::st_intersects))
    
    # generate frequencies matching unique gadm layer identifiers and drop point geometry structures safely
    counts_df <- sf_joined %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(GID_3)) %>%
      dplyr::count(GID_3, name = "hh_count")
    
    # bind counts back onto geometry frame and format text explicitly inside plotmath expressions
    annotated_sf <- kenya_wards_sf %>%
      dplyr::left_join(counts_df, by = "GID_3") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(hh_count)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(display_label = base::paste0("atop(bold('", NAME_3, "'), '(N = ", hh_count, ")')"))
    
  } else if (group_by == "county") {
    # spatially join household coordinates to identify active county parents
    sf_joined <- suppressMessages(sf::st_join(sf_df, kenya_counties_sf, join = sf::st_intersects))
    
    # generate frequencies matching unique gadm layer identifiers and drop point geometry structures safely
    counts_df <- sf_joined %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(GID_1)) %>%
      dplyr::count(GID_1, name = "hh_count")
    
    # bind counts back onto geometry frame and format text explicitly inside plotmath expressions
    annotated_sf <- kenya_counties_sf %>%
      dplyr::left_join(counts_df, by = "GID_1") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(hh_count)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(display_label = base::paste0("atop(bold('", NAME_1, "'), '(N = ", hh_count, ")')"))
  } else {
    base::stop("invalid group_by selection, please configure as either 'ward' or 'county'")
  }
  
  # extract geographic interior centroids calculated from the largest continuous landmass polygon space
  label_points <- base::suppressWarnings(sf::st_centroid(annotated_sf, of_largest_polygon = TRUE))
  label_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(label_points)
  
  annotated_sf$label_lon <- label_coords[, 1]
  annotated_sf$label_lat <- label_coords[, 2]
  
  # map the underlying geographic map framework and lay labels over top
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    # render detailed ward lines using thin soft pink profiles
    ggplot2::geom_sf(
      data = kenya_wards_sf,
      fill = "#fff5f6",
      color = "#FFE4E8",
      linewidth = 0.3,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    # overlay the main county line borders using a thicker soft pink profile
    ggplot2::geom_sf(
      data = kenya_counties_sf,
      fill = NA,
      color = "#FFB7C5",
      linewidth = 1.0,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    # drop authentic unicode location pin symbols directly locked onto the precise internal centroids
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = annotated_sf,
      ggplot2::aes(x = label_lon, y = label_lat),
      label = "\U0001F4CD",
      size = 5,
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    # repel text descriptions outside regional boundaries using mathematical parsing to force bold styling
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = annotated_sf,
      ggplot2::aes(x = label_lon, y = label_lat, label = display_label),
      color = "#722F37",
      size = font_size,
      parse = TRUE,
      box.padding = 1.2,
      point.padding = 0.3,
      max.overlaps = Inf,
      arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.015, "npc"), type = "closed"),
      segment.color = "#722F37",
      segment.size = 0.4
    )
  
  # format layout grids and text descriptions
  p <- p +
    # enforce true spatial map coordinates and automatically scale map frame bounds to whole country shape
    ggplot2::coord_sf(crs = 4326) +
    # inject a minimal clean compass style north arrow matching the soft pink layout color at the custom location
    ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(
      location = compass_pos, 
      which_north = "true",
      style = ggspatial::north_arrow_minimal(line_col = "#FFB7C5", fill = "#FFB7C5")
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = "Longitude",
      y = "Latitude"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 13),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.box = "vertical",
      # clean background panels
      panel.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#fff9fa", color = NA)
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```



## household count plot interactive

```{r function-plot_household_counts_interactive}
#' plot interactive household count markers using real location pin icons positioned safely inside boundaries
#'
#' @param data dataframe containing household level records
#' @param lat_col character name of the latitude column
#' @param lon_col character name of the longitude column
#' @param group_by character administrative grouping scale choice, either 'ward' or 'county'
#' @param compass_pos character layout position for the north arrow, defaults to 'topleft'
#'
#' @returns a leaflet map widget object
#' @importFrom dplyr filter group_by summarise n count left_join mutate
#' @importFrom sf st_as_sf st_join st_point_on_surface st_coordinates st_drop_geometry
#' @importFrom geodata gadm
#' @importFrom leaflet leaflet addPolygons addMarkers labelOptions leafletOptions addControl
#' @importFrom htmltools HTML
#' @export
plot_household_counts_interactive <- function(data, lat_col, lon_col, group_by = "ward", compass_pos = "topleft") {
  
  # isolate coordinates and filter out missing records
  plot_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[lat_col]]), !is.na(.data[[lon_col]]))
  
  # transform the raw dataframe into a coordinate spatial sf object (wgs84 projection)
  sf_df <- sf::st_as_sf(
    plot_df, 
    coords = c(lon_col, lat_col), 
    crs = 4326
  )
  
  # dynamically download the official boundaries from gadm database
  kenya_spatvector_l1 <- geodata::gadm(country = "KEN", level = 1, path = base::tempdir())
  kenya_counties_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(kenya_spatvector_l1)
  
  kenya_spatvector_l3 <- geodata::gadm(country = "KEN", level = 3, path = base::tempdir())
  kenya_wards_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(kenya_spatvector_l3)
  
  # aggregate counts and map tracking labels based on chosen administrative group scale
  if (group_by == "ward") {
    # spatially join household coordinates to identify active ward parents
    sf_joined <- base::suppressMessages(sf::st_join(sf_df, kenya_wards_sf, join = sf::st_intersects))
    
    # generate frequencies matching unique gadm layer identifiers and drop point geometry structures safely
    counts_df <- sf_joined %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(GID_3)) %>%
      dplyr::count(GID_3, name = "hh_count")
    
    # bind counts back onto geometry frame and format clean text combinations for interactive hover flags
    annotated_sf <- kenya_wards_sf %>%
      dplyr::left_join(counts_df, by = "GID_3") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(hh_count)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        hover_label = base::paste0("<strong>Ward:</strong> ", NAME_3, "<br><strong>Households:</strong> ", hh_count)
      )
    
  } else if (group_by == "county") {
    # spatially join household coordinates to identify active county parents
    sf_joined <- base::suppressMessages(sf::st_join(sf_df, kenya_counties_sf, join = sf::st_intersects))
    
    # generate frequencies matching unique gadm layer identifiers and drop point geometry structures safely
    counts_df <- sf_joined %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(GID_1)) %>%
      dplyr::count(GID_1, name = "hh_count")
    
    # bind counts back onto geometry frame and format clean text combinations for interactive hover flags
    annotated_sf <- kenya_counties_sf %>%
      dplyr::left_join(counts_df, by = "GID_1") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(hh_count)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        hover_label = base::paste0("<strong>County:</strong> ", NAME_1, "<br><strong>Households:</strong> ", hh_count)
      )
  } else {
    base::stop("invalid group_by selection, please configure as either 'ward' or 'county'")
  }
  
  # extract spatial surface coordinates guaranteed to be mathematically inside the polygon boundaries
  label_points <- base::suppressWarnings(sf::st_point_on_surface(annotated_sf))
  label_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(label_points)
  
  annotated_sf$label_lon <- label_coords[, 1]
  annotated_sf$label_lat <- label_coords[, 2]
  
  # design a custom html soft pink compass ornament using a safe portable unicode escape sequence for the arrow (\u25b2)
  compass_html <- htmltools::HTML('
    <div style="
      text-align: center; 
      font-family: sans-serif; 
      color: #FFB7C5; 
      background: rgba(255, 245, 246, 0.8); 
      padding: 6px 10px; 
      border-radius: 4px; 
      border: 2px solid #FFB7C5;
      font-weight: bold;
    ">
      <div style="font-size: 20px; line-height: 1;">\u25B2</div>
      <div style="font-size: 13px; margin-top: 2px;">N</div>
    </div>
  ')
  
  # initialize a clean leaflet map structure with zooming rules
  lf <- leaflet::leaflet(options = leaflet::leafletOptions(minZoom = 5, maxZoom = 14)) %>%
    # render detailed background ward lines using a very clean subtle light pink fill
    leaflet::addPolygons(
      data = kenya_wards_sf,
      fillColor = "#fffafb",
      fillOpacity = 0.6,
      color = "#FFE4E8",
      weight = 1,
      opacity = 0.8,
      group = "Wards"
    ) %>%
    # overlay the main county line borders using a thicker soft pink profile
    leaflet::addPolygons(
      data = kenya_counties_sf,
      fillColor = "transparent",
      color = "#FFB7C5",
      weight = 1.8,
      opacity = 1.0,
      group = "Counties"
    ) %>%
    # anchor the custom styled compass ornament securely to the canvas UI
    leaflet::addControl(html = compass_html, position = compass_pos) %>%
    # render native location pin icon markers that surface rich html label strings upon mouse hover
    leaflet::addMarkers(
      data = annotated_sf,
      lng = ~label_lon,
      lat = ~label_lat,
      label = ~base::lapply(hover_label, htmltools::HTML),
      labelOptions = leaflet::labelOptions(
        style = base::list(
          "font-family" = "sans-serif",
          "font-size" = "12px",
          "color" = "#722F37",
          "border-color" = "#FFB7C5"
        )
      )
    )
  
  return(lf)
}
```

## get partner beneficiaries

```{r function-get_partner_beneficiaries}
#' filter and deduplicate beneficiary logs by agency partner
#'
#' @param df dataframe containing master registry logs
#' @param partner character keyword used to identify the target agency, defaults to 'pgi'
#' @param columns character vector of column names to distinct by, defaults to c('ben_name', 'ben_id_number')
#'
#' @returns a deduplicated dataframe containing partner specific records
#' @importFrom dplyr filter distinct across all_of
#' @export
get_partner_beneficiaries <- function(df = df_out, partner = "pgi", columns = c("ben_name", "ben_id_number")) {
  
  # match agency keyword and remove duplicates based on dynamic columns argument configuration
  processed_df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(base::grepl(partner, enum_egency, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(columns)), .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  return(processed_df)
}
```

```{r function-check_disability}
#' validate and recode household disability flags based on repeat group ages
#'
#' @param df_out dataframe containing the main household data
#' @param df_disab dataframe containing the individual repeat group data
#' @param uuid_col character string of the ID column name in df_out (defaults to "uuid")
#' @param age numeric lower age limit
#'
#' @returns an updated version of df_out with corrected disability flags
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' # lower case comments without dots or dashes
#' # create dummy main dataset
#' main_df <- data.frame(
#'   uuid = c("hh_1", "hh_2", "hh_3"),
#'   HHM_disability = c("yes", "yes", "no"),
#'   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
#' )
#' 
#' # create dummy repeat group dataset
#' repeat_df <- data.frame(
#'   `_uuid` = c("hh_1", "hh_1", "hh_2", "hh_2", "hh_3"),
#'   HHM_disability = c("yes", "no", "yes", "yes", "no"),
#'   prot_disability_ind_age = c(1, 35, 2, 1, 40),
#'   stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
#'   check.names = FALSE
#' )
#' 
#' # run the function
#' output_df <- check_disability(main_df, repeat_df, uuid_col = "uuid")
check_disability <- function(df_out, df_disab, uuid_col = "uuid", age = 6) {
  
  # step 1: isolate active disability rows and find the maximum age per household
  hh_max_disab_age <- df_disab %>%
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(base::tolower(HHM_disability), "yes")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(`_uuid`) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      max_age = base::max(prot_disability_ind_age, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # step 2: extract household IDs where the maximum disabled age is 2 or under
  infant_only_uuids <- hh_max_disab_age %>%
    dplyr::filter(max_age < age) %>%
    dplyr::pull(`_uuid`)
  
  # step 3: calculate diagnostics for console visibility
  total_infant_only_hh <- base::length(infant_only_uuids)
  
  # step 4: recode the main dataset if any invalid target households exist
  df_out_updated <- df_out %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # lower case comments without dots or dashes
      HHM_disability = dplyr::if_else(
        .data[[uuid_col]] %in% infant_only_uuids,
        "no",
        HHM_disability
      )
    )
  
  # step 5: print diagnostic feedback to the console safely
  base::message("--- disability check summary ---")
  base::message(base::sprintf("households with active disability loops: %d", base::nrow(hh_max_disab_age)))
  base::message(base::sprintf("households where all disabled members are < %d (total: %d)", age, total_infant_only_hh))
  
  if (total_infant_only_hh > 0) {
    base::message("action: invalid household flags successfully recoded to 'no'")
  } else {
    base::message("action: no adjustments needed, all household flags are structurally valid")
  }
  base::message("--------------------------------")
  
  return(df_out_updated)
}
```

## calculate disability counts

```{r function-calculate_disability_counts}
#' calculate a row level individual disability indicator
#'
#' @param data dataframe containing the individual disability columns
#' @param disability_cols character vector of column names representing the domains
#'
#' @returns an integer vector of 1s and 0s indicating if the individual has any disability
#' @export
calculate_disability_counts <- function(data, 
                                        disability_cols = c(
                                          "level_seeing_disability",
                                          "level_hearing_disability",
                                          "level_selfcare_disability",
                                          "level_remembering_disability",
                                          "level_walking_disability",
                                          "level_communicating_disability"
                                        )) {
  
  # extract target columns to safely check row conditions
  subset_matrix <- data %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(disability_cols))
  
  # match case-insensitively against the exact literal strings provided
  # lower case comments without dots
  match_matrix <- base::apply(subset_matrix, 2, function(col) {
    stringr::str_to_lower(base::as.character(col)) %in% c("some difficulty", "a lot of difficulty", "cannot do at all")
  })
  
  # collapse individual domains down to a single binary indicator per row
  dplyr::if_else(base::rowSums(match_matrix, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, 1L, 0L)
}

```

## hh disability burden  counts

counts multiple forms of disability among household members.

```{r function-calculate_hh_disability_counts}
#' calculate the total number of disabled individuals at the household level
#'
#' @param data dataframe containing the individual disability columns and a household identifier
#' @param hh_id_col character name of the column storing the unique household id
#' @param disability_cols character vector of column names representing the domains
#'
#' @returns an integer vector representing the total disabled household members for each row
#' @export
calculate_hh_disability_counts <- function(data, 
                                           hh_id_col = "uuid",
                                           disability_cols = c(
                                             "level_seeing_disability",
                                             "level_hearing_disability",
                                             "level_selfcare_disability",
                                             "level_remembering_disability",
                                             "level_walking_disability",
                                             "level_communicating_disability"
                                           )) {
  
  # extract target columns to safely check row conditions
  subset_matrix <- data %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(disability_cols))
  
  # match case-insensitively against the exact literal choices provided
  # lower case comments without dots
  match_matrix <- base::apply(subset_matrix, 2, function(col) {
    stringr::str_to_lower(base::as.character(col)) %in% c("some difficulty", "a lot of difficulty", "cannot do at all")
  })
  
  # collapse individual domains down to a single binary indicator per row
  ind_disabled <- dplyr::if_else(base::rowSums(match_matrix, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, 1L, 0L)
  
  # create a temporary tracking block to calculate the broadcasted household sums safely
  result_vector <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(temp_ind_disabled = ind_disabled) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[hh_id_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(total_disabled_in_hh = base::sum(temp_ind_disabled, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::pull(total_disabled_in_hh)
  
  return(result_vector)
}
```


## recode early childhood disability

```{r function-recode_early_childhood_disability}
#' reset disability columns based on age thresholds
#'
#' @param data dataframe containing the disability and age columns
#' @param disability_cols character vector of column names representing the domains
#' @param age_col character name of the column storing age values
#'
#' @returns a modified dataframe with recoded disability entries for children under 6
#' @export
recode_early_childhood_disability <- function(data,
                                              disability_cols = c(
                                                "level_seeing_disability",
                                                "level_hearing_disability",
                                                "level_selfcare_disability",
                                                "level_remembering_disability",
                                                "level_walking_disability",
                                                "level_communicating_disability"
                                              ),
                                              age_col = "prot_disability_ind_age") {
  data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(disability_cols),
        ~ dplyr::if_else(
          # check if age exists and falls below the 6 year target threshold
          !base::is.na(.data[[age_col]]) & .data[[age_col]] < 6,
          "No difficulty",
          # preserve the original cell contents if criteria are not met
          base::as.character(.x)
        )
      )
    )
}
```

```{r function-recode_factor_to_character}
#' recode factors to character

#'

#' @examples
#' \dontrun{recode_factor_to_character()}
recode_factor_to_character <- function(x) {

      dplyr::where(labelled::is.labelled),

        base::as.character()
```
