## get dupes with name

```{r function-get_dupes_with_name}
#' get duplicate rows, track the checked field, and subset down to designated columns via an argument
#'
#' @param data a dataframe or tibble
#' @param col the unquoted column name to check for duplicates, defaults to ben_name
#' @param cols_select a list of unquoted column expressions to select, defaults to a predefined set
#'
#' @returns a filtered and pruned dataframe of duplicate rows
#' @importFrom rlang ensyms exprs
#' @importFrom janitor get_dupes
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate select
#' @export
get_dupes_with_name <- function(
    data, 
    col = ben_name, 
    cols_select = rlang::exprs(county, enum_egency, enum_name,ben_name, ben_id_number,reg_num, dup_col, uuid)
) {
  
  # capture the checking columns safely as a list of symbols
  col_syms <- rlang::ensyms(col)
  
  # convert the captured symbols into character strings for label grouping
  col_strings <- base::as.character(col_syms)
  combined_label <- base::paste(col_strings, collapse = ", ")
  
  # run the janitor deduplication filter across all target symbols and append the tracking string
  processed_df <- data %>%
    janitor::get_dupes(!!!col_syms) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dup_col = combined_label)
  
  # inject and combine the checked column symbols directly into the selection expression list
  final_select_exprs <- base::unique(c(col_syms, cols_select))
  
  # evaluate the complete unified selection expression list dynamically
  result <- processed_df %>%
    dplyr::select(!!!final_select_exprs)
  
  return(result)
}
```

## label data 

```{r function-label_kobo_columns}
#' replace data column names with question labels from a kobo asset form metadata structure
#'
#' @param data dataframe containing the downloaded survey submission records
#' @param kobo_asset a labelled list/dataframe compiled from the xlsform or robotoolbox
#' @param lang character optional specific language label column to use if multilingual, e.g., 'English (en)'
#'
#' @returns dataframe with renamed columns
#' @importFrom purrr map_chr
#' @importFrom dplyr rename_with everything
#' @export
label_kobo_columns <- function(data, kobo_asset, lang = NULL) {
  
  # extract the label attributes from the kobo asset columns
  label_mapping <- purrr::map_chr(kobo_asset, function(col) {
    lbls <- attr(col, "label")
    if (is.null(lbls)) return(NA_character_)
    
    # handle multilingual assets where labels might be a named vector
    if (!is.null(lang) && lang %in% names(lbls)) {
      return(lbls[lang])
    }
    
    # default to the first available label if no language is specified
    return(lbls[1])
  })
  
  # drop missing or empty labels to keep original column names where mapping fails
  label_mapping <- label_mapping[!is.na(label_mapping) & label_mapping != ""]
  
  # rename columns using the named vector mapping lookup
  result <- data %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(
      ~ ifelse(.x %in% names(label_mapping), label_mapping[.x], .x),
      dplyr::everything()
    )
  
  return(result)
}
```

## read xls form as kobo labelled assset

```{r function-read_xlsform_asset}
#' read an xlsform file and compile it into a kobo asset metadata list
#'
#' @param xlsform_path character. path to your local xlsform .xlsx or .xls file
#'
#' @returns a named list structured exactly like a robotoolbox kobo_asset object
#' @importFrom readxl read_excel
#' @importFrom dplyr filter select
#' @export
read_xlsform_asset <- function(xlsform_path) {
  
  # 1. read the survey design sheet from the workbook
  survey_sheet <- readxl::read_excel(xlsform_path, sheet = "survey")
  
  # 2. filter down to rows that represent real questions with names
  survey_questions <- survey_sheet %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(name))
  
  # 3. isolate all available label columns (handles multilingual headers like label::English (en))
  label_cols <- names(survey_questions)[stringr::str_starts(names(survey_questions), "label")]
  
  # if no complex language markers exist, default back to standard label
  if (length(label_cols) == 0 && "label" %in% names(survey_questions)) {
    label_cols <- "label"
  }
  
  # 4. dynamically build the mocked asset list structure
  kobo_asset <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(survey_questions))) {
    col_name <- survey_questions$name[i]
    
    # gather all label strings for the current question row
    labels_vec <- c()
    for (lbl_col in label_cols) {
      lbl_val <- survey_questions[[lbl_col]][i]
      
      if (!is.na(lbl_val) && lbl_val != "") {
        # normalize name format: strip 'label::' prefix if present to isolate language key
        lang_key <- stringr::str_remove(lbl_col, "^label::")
        if (lang_key == "label") lang_key <- "default"
        
        labels_vec[lang_key] <- lbl_val
      }
    }
    
    # structure each element as an empty mock column container holding label metadata
    col_trigger <- list()
    attr(col_trigger, "label") <- labels_vec
    
    kobo_asset[[col_name]] <- col_trigger
  }
  
  return(kobo_asset)
}
```


## convert kobo header labels to column values

```{r function-convert_excel_headers}
#' convert labeled excel headers to kobo code/value headers using form schema
#'
#' @param target_df data.frame. the raw excel data frame with text headers (df)
#' @param project_id character. kobo project uid
#' @param url character. Kobotoolbox url
#' @param token character. project token
#'
#' @returns a data frame with clean value headers matching df_lab
#' @export
convert_excel_headers <- function(
    target_df,
    url = Sys.getenv("kobo_url2"),
    project_id = Sys.getenv("mpca_id"),
    token = Sys.getenv("kobo_token")
) {
  
  # 1. pull the asset form schema from the api
  robotoolbox::kobo_setup(url = url, token = token)
  asset <- robotoolbox::kobo_asset(project_id)
  form_schema <- robotoolbox::kobo_form(asset)
  
  # 2. isolate question row rows with non-empty names and labels
  # clean the labels exactly how R cleans column names upon import
  mapping_dict <- form_schema %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(name), !is.na(label)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      clean_label = janitor::make_clean_names(label)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(clean_label, name) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(clean_label, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    tibble::deframe() # turns it into a named vector: c(clean_label = "name")
  
  # 3. safely handle complex select_multiple columns
  # kobo appends choice suffixes to the question stem for binary choice columns
  # e.g., 'what_is_the_current_source_of_livelihood..._formal_employment' -> 'livelihood_source_f_employment'
  current_names <- names(target_df)
  new_names <- sapply(current_names, function(col_name) {
    
    # direct hit check against standard questions
    if (col_name %in% names(mapping_dict)) {
      return(mapping_dict[[col_name]])
    }
    
    # check if this column is a split choice from a select_multiple question block
    # matches the longest matching stem and finds the underlying code value
    matches <- sapply(names(mapping_dict), function(lbl) stringr::str_starts(col_name, fixed(lbl)))
    if (any(matches)) {
      best_fit_lbl <- names(which(matches))[which.max(nchar(names(which(matches))))]
      base_code_name <- mapping_dict[[best_fit_lbl]]
      
      # extract just the choice suffix appended to the end of the text label
      suffix <- stringr::str_remove(col_name, paste0("^", regexp_quote(best_fit_lbl), "_?"))
      
      # reconstruct the backend column name string structure
      return(paste0(base_code_name, "_", suffix))
    }
    
    # return original name if no match found (e.g. metadata markers like uuid, start, end)
    return(col_name)
  })
  
  # 4. assign the translated backend names onto your excel dataset
  names(target_df) <- unname(new_names)
  
  # 5. a quick universal adjustment pass for project-agnostic group paths
  # fixes remnants of section wrappers if your schema lists them cleanly
  target_df <- target_df %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace_all(.x, "\\.", "_"))
  
  return(target_df)
}

# helper function to escape characters for safe regex evaluation
regexp_quote <- function(kv) {
  gsub("([.[{}()^*+?|\\^$])", "\\\\\\1", kv)
}
```

## label with xlsform

```{r function-label_with_xlsform}
#' convert and label an excel export using xlsform workbook sheets
#'
#' @param data_df data.frame. the raw exported kobo data with label headers (df)
#' @param xlsform_path character. path to your local xlsform .xlsx workbook
#'
#' @returns a clean data frame with code headers and labeled categorical values
#' @export
label_with_xlsform <- function(data_df, xlsform_path) {
  
  # 1. read the design sheets from the xlsform template
  survey_sheet  <- readxl::read_excel(xlsform_path, sheet = "survey")
  choices_sheet <- readxl::read_excel(xlsform_path, sheet = "choices")
  
  # 2. handle column header conversion (label string -> code name)
  # ensure we only target actual question rows with values
  survey_clean <- survey_sheet %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(name), !is.na(label)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(clean_label = janitor::make_clean_names(label))
  
  # generate a named mapping dictionary vector: c(clean_label = "name")
  header_dict <- survey_clean %>%
    dplyr::select(clean_label, name) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(clean_label, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    tibble::deframe()
  
  current_names <- names(data_df)
  new_names <- sapply(current_names, function(col_name) {
    # check for a direct match
    if (col_name %in% names(header_dict)) {
      return(header_dict[[col_name]])
    }
    
    # check for select_multiple split columns
    # loops through labels to find if col_name starts with a known stem label
    matches <- sapply(names(header_dict), function(lbl) stringr::str_starts(col_name, fixed(lbl)))
    if (any(matches)) {
      best_fit_lbl <- names(which(matches))[which.max(nchar(names(which(matches))))]
      base_code_name <- header_dict[[best_fit_lbl]]
      
      # isolate the text choice suffix and append it back to the clean code stem
      suffix <- stringr::str_remove(col_name, paste0("^", gsub("([.[{}()^*+?|\\^$])", "\\\\\\1", best_fit_lbl), "_?"))
      return(paste0(base_code_name, "_", suffix))
    }
    return(col_name)
  })
  
  names(data_df) <- unname(new_names)
  
  # 3. handle categorical row value labeling
  # extract the choice list links from the question types (e.g., 'select_one list_name')
  questions_with_choices <- survey_clean %>%
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(type, "select_")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      list_name = stringr::str_extract(type, "(?<=select_[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,100}[:space:]).*")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(list_name)) %>%
    dplyr::select(name, list_name)
  
  # build dictionaries for each choice group inside the choices sheet
  choices_clean <- choices_sheet %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(list_name), !is.na(name), !is.na(label)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      name = as.character(name),
      lookup_key = paste0(list_name, "__", name)
    )
  
  choices_lookup <- choices_clean %>%
    dplyr::select(lookup_key, label) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(lookup_key, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    tibble::deframe()
  
  # create a question-to-list mapping vector
  q_to_list <- questions_with_choices %>% tibble::deframe()
  
  # 4. map row values across matching select columns
  data_df <- data_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), function(col) {
      col_name <- dplyr::cur_column()
      
      if (col_name %in% names(q_to_list)) {
        list_name <- q_to_list[[col_name]]
        col_str <- as.character(col)
        
        # construct lookup codes: listname__value
        lookup_keys <- paste0(list_name, "__", col_str)
        
        col_mapped <- dplyr::if_else(
          lookup_keys %in% names(choices_lookup),
          choices_lookup[lookup_keys],
          col_str
        )
        return(col_mapped)
      }
      return(col)
    }))
  
  # universal pass to remove group dot leftovers if present
  data_df <- data_df %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace_all(.x, "\\.", "_"))
  
  return(data_df)
}
```


## parse hh size

```{r function-parse_hhsize}
#' Parse and extract household size as an integer vector
#'
#' This function sanitizes a character vector of household sizes containing
#' mixed entries (e.g., "5(3F:2M)", "Size 9", "s6"), discarding data entry 
#' noise like phone numbers, registration IDs, or full names.
#'
#' @param x character. A vector containing raw household size values.
#'
#' @returns An integer vector of clean household sizes.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' clean_sizes <- parse_hhsize(df$ben_hhsize)
#' }
parse_hhsize <- function(x) {
  
  # convert vector to character and make uniform for regex matching
  working_vec <- stringr::str_trim(as.character(x))
  working_vec <- stringr::str_to_lower(working_vec)
  
  # perform structural parsing based on prioritized text patterns
  clean_vec <- dplyr::case_when(
    # extract leading total digits before bracketed breakdowns: '5(3f:2m)' -> 5
    stringr::str_detect(working_vec, "^\\d+\\s*\\(") ~ 
      stringr::str_extract(working_vec, "^\\d+"),
    
    # isolate strings with descriptive prefix layout: 'size 9' or 'fs- 5' -> 9 or 5
    stringr::str_detect(working_vec, "^(size|fs|fs-|s)\\s*\\d+$") ~ 
      stringr::str_extract(working_vec, "\\d+"),
    
    # isolate strings with standalone gender suffix layout: '3m' or '6f' -> 3 or 6
    stringr::str_detect(working_vec, "^\\d+[mf]$") ~ 
      stringr::str_extract(working_vec, "^\\d+"),
    
    # safely convert known text noise, registration IDs, and phone numbers to NA
    stringr::str_detect(working_vec, "-|\\s[a-z]|^07") ~ NA_character_,
    
    # keep remaining clean structures intact
    TRUE ~ working_vec
  )
  
  # return final casted integer vector
  return(as.integer(clean_vec))
}
```


## run sampling schemes

```{r function-run_sample}
#' run sampling schemes
#'
#' @param df_frame dataframe of sampling frame
#' @param df_sample_n dataframe of sample size
#' @param dir charcter. of output path
#' @param type charcter. monitoring stage 
#' @param name charcter. file name for otput
#'
#' @returns NULL
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{run_sample()}
run_sample <- function(df_frame, df_sample_n, dir = Sys.getenv("dir_unocha"), type = "PDM", name = "FDG"){
  large_villages <- df_frame %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      .by = c(county, village)
    ) %>%
    filter(n >= 50)
  
  ds <- df_frame %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl("^vuln", eligibility)) %>%
    filter(
      village %in% large_villages$village
    )
  
  dd <- draw_pps_sample(
    data = ds,
    allocation_df = df_sample_n,
    
  )
  
  cols <- c("county",
            "subloc",
            "ward",
            "village$",
            "ben_name",
            "ben_id_number",
            "reg_num$",
            "proxy_first",
            "proxy_second",
            "proxy_num"
            
  )
  sample_out <- dd %>%
    select(grep(paste(cols, collapse = "|"), names(.)))
  out_lst <- split(sample_out, sample_out$county) %>%
    purrr::set_names(sort(unique(sample_out$county)))
  
  acheck::write_list_to_excel(
    out_lst,
    file_path = file.path(dir, type, "sample", paste0(name, "_sample_", Sys.Date(), ".xlsx"))
  )
}

```
